[What is Smart Locker?](#accordion-93a4467b-9d68-4006-a48b-bfc6e2c2051e "What is Smart Locker")  
Smart locker is an automated self-service system, it allows bank clients to access their lockers at any time of the day 24\7.  
[How Customers can apply for the locker service?](#accordion-f6ec3f03-a08e-481c-9819-7f4e83ac533b "How Customers can apply for the locker service")  
Subscription to Smart Locker facility requires a minimum relationship requirement  
[Where can customers apply for the smart locker](#accordion-a272a77e-51a0-489e-892b-495ea4086b9e "Where can customers apply for the smart locker")  
The smart lockers are available only at Jumeirah Branch (Al Wasl road).  
[How does it work?](#accordion-c90e31e6-d5ef-4280-9e73-a91139392539 "How does it work")  
A. Subscribe to smart deposits lockers  
B. With the fingerprint reader, you can access to the branch and smart locker lobby area  
C. Insert the key card to access the service room.  
D. Re-enter the key access card in the service unit, enter the PIN and place your finger on the biometric scanner  
E. Select your locker number  
F. The Smart Locker robot will select the right box and deliver it to you  
G. Open the box with your physical key  
H. After use, close the box with your physical key and press Deposit

# Five things they didn’t teach you about money in school  
14 October 2025  
[Share](javascript:void(0); "Share")  
![fivethingstheydidntteachyouaboutmoneyinschool](/-/media/enbd/images/knowledge-hub/five_things_they_didnt_teach.jpg?la=en&h=600&w=800&hash=C5BA2FC6F4BE09396EA6B870DE8BA276)  
#####  
Ask any teenager what they are taught about money in school and the answer is almost always the same: ‘Nothing’. That’s a missed opportunity, because understanding saving and investing early is one of the most powerful ways to build wealth and open the doors to financial independence. In fact, a quick poll among young people showed that their top money question was simple but telling: ‘How can I become a millionaire?’  
Fair question. Let’s dive in.
title: Five things they didn’t teach you about money in school
section: Five things they didn’t teach you about money in school

text:
Five things they didn’t teach you about money in school > **How can I become a millionaire?**

## **How can I become a millionaire?**  
‘I’ll never save that much!’ Is that you? Wrong. Becoming a millionaire is absolutely possible. You just need to start early, invest wisely and make a habit of it.  
**Ever heard of the 50-30-20 rule?** All it means is that you spend 50% of your income on essentials (rent, food etc.); 30% on wants (things you want, but can do without), and save 20%. The 20% you sock away is what will make you rich – eventually.  
Starting young gives you the risk appetite advantage. What that means is that when you’re young, you can take more risk. So, find out where you can get the best returns for your money and you’ll be surprised how compounded interest accelerates your savings.  
Here’s a simple calculation based on a salary of 15,000:  
Let’s save 20% of that following the 50-30-20 rule.
20% of 15,000 = 3,000
We’re going to save 3,000 every month for 25 years.
3,000 x 12 x 25 = 900,000
To this, add a conservative rate of return (or compounded interest rate) of 2% over 25 years and you’ve hit your million-dirham target already.  
Remember, your income will increase over 25 years, so you will likely hit your target much earlier. Also, interest rates, or returns on investment depend on where you invest your money. You can earn much more than just 2% on capital guaranteed investment schemes, mutual funds and so on. Just speak to your bank advisor for more information.  
**Rule number 1.** Follow the 50-30-20 faithfully. Start early.
title: Five things they didn’t teach you about money in school

text:
Five things they didn’t teach you about money in school > **The benefits of using a credit card responsibly**

## **The benefits of using a credit card responsibly**  
Credit cards are a great tool if used responsibly. They give you a whole 30 days of credit for free, and what’s more, they allow you to buy stuff on credit and pay back in easy instalments. So, you can enjoy today what you would have normally had to wait months for. What’s wrong with that? Nothing, but like so much else, it can go wrong if used irresponsibly.  
Easy access to credit can tempt you to live beyond your means. If you fall into the trap of paying back only the minimum balance, the high interest rates on credit cards will sink you deeper into debt every month.  
**Rule number 2.** Always clear your credit card bill every month.
title: Five things they didn’t teach you about money in school
section: **The benefits of using a credit card responsibly**

text:
Five things they didn’t teach you about money in school > **Investing**

## **Investing**  
Investing is a skill. Be it picking a great investment plan, investing in realty, stocks, shares, or trading. Investing is one of the most financially rewarding things you can learn how to do.  
Managing money is a life skill. It must be learnt. And it’s never too late. Read about it, talk to experts, subscribe to newsletters. Wisen up.  
A few things you can consider investing in: savings plans, real estate, mutual funds, capital-guaranteed funds, stocks and shares or even CFDs (look that up).  
Knowledge is key, so learn everything you can before you venture into an investment.  
**Rule number 3.** Invest your money wisely for better returns. Knowledge is key. Learn.
title: Five things they didn’t teach you about money in school

text:
Five things they didn’t teach you about money in school > **How to open and manage a bank account**

## **How to open and manage a bank account**  
A [**minor savings account**](https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/help-and-support/open-a-minor-account?source=search), opened by guardian at a young age can teach pre-teens and early teens how to save early and give them the thrill of seeing their savings grow – slowly and steadily. That habit will likely always stay with them.  
Opening a bank account is so much simpler these days. You can even open an instant account online without having to go to the bank at all. Learn about the [**current and savings accounts**](https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/accounts), [**deposits**](https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/accounts) and [**banking packages**](https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/banking-packages). Consider a fixed deposit with auto deductions every month, or invest in a gold deposit which gives you the advantage of investing in gold without holding the physical asset. Learn more about interest rates and investment plans. Just plant your money and watch it grow.  
This doesn’t mean you become a scrooge and don’t spend on fun. Just make sure you save some, and you’re good.  
**Rule number 4.** Open a savings account. Refer to Rule 1.
title: Five things they didn’t teach you about money in school
section: **How to open and manage a bank account**

text:
Five things they didn’t teach you about money in school > **There’s no such thing as easy money**

## **There’s no such thing as easy money**  
Last, but not least, beware of get-rich quick schemes – they’re plenty of scammers out there. Regularly saving, investing and watching your money grow, helping your dreams materialise, is not just gratifying – it’s a safe, time-tested way to grow your wealth and gain financial independence early in life. Sure, you can get lucky with the lottery or an inheritance, but for the vast majority, saving and investing wisely really can’t go wrong.  
**Rule number 5.** Be prepared to put in the work. There’s no such thing as easy money.  
Good luck and may you be a millionaire sooner than you think you can.

## Quick Answers  
[Am I eligible for an Installment Payment Plan?](#accordion-d005dbab-c436-4f33-9a4e-a64db2a085cf "Am I eligible for an Installment Payment Plan")  
You can convert purchases worth a minimum of 750 from your latest statement and current billing cycle into Installment Payment Plans.  
[Can I still earn reward points if I convert a transaction to an Installment Payment Plan with interest?](#accordion-d3a6288b-905a-458d-aaeb-12e47201cd12 "Can I still earn reward points if I convert a transaction to an Installment Payment Plan with interest")  
Yes, you will still earn reward points if you convert your transaction to a regular Installment Payment Plan.  
[Are there any processing fees for installment plans?](#accordion-ec807f77-b055-479d-b85e-e13eb4f307b9 "Are there any processing fees for installment plans")  
Regular Installment Payment Plan, Balance Conversion, and Loan on Card don’t have a processing fee, but a nominal interest rate applies based on your credit card history and usage.
With the 0% interest Installment Payment Plan there could be a one-time processing fee of 51.45 (inclusive of VAT) per transaction. For more details, read more about our [**fees and charges**](/-/media/enbd/files/others/fees-and-charges/cards/emiratesnbd_credit_card_fees_charges.pdf).

text:
Installment Payment Plan Request | Emirates NBD > Quick Answers

Regular Installment Payment Plan, Balance Conversion, and Loan on Card don’t have a processing fee, but a nominal interest rate applies based on your credit card history and usage.
With the 0% interest Installment Payment Plan there could be a one-time processing fee of 51.45 (inclusive of VAT) per transaction. For more details, read more about our [**fees and charges**](/-/media/enbd/files/others/fees-and-charges/cards/emiratesnbd_credit_card_fees_charges.pdf).  
[Can I cancel my installment plan?](#accordion-1917004c-6057-48a7-96f9-8893b203d62a "Can I cancel my installment plan")  
Yes, you can cancel your installment plan through Mobile Banking and Online Banking.
Before cancelling your plan, you will have to settle the remaining principal outstanding plus a foreclosure fee of 1% of the principal outstanding and 5% VAT.  
[I want to follow up on a previous request.](#accordion-0cc32ca7-1a40-49bd-9016-8ff3f9457279 "I want to follow up on a previous request.")  
You can track your previous request by calling us on [**+971 600 54 0000**](tel:+971600540000) and when prompted, say ‘follow up on my request’.

[Am I eligible for a Priority Banking Current Account?](#accordion-27bc4dff-2770-4b0e-a111-8f943a6abc14 "Am I eligible for a Priority Banking Current Account")  
Our Current Accounts are open to new and existing customers of all nationalities.  
To apply you must be:  
* 18 years or older (or a minor with your legal guardian’s signature)
* UAE residence visa holder
* Priority Banking customer or meet the Priority Banking threshold  
[What do I need to open a Priority Banking Current Account?](#accordion-2fb3616d-a312-4a93-8a96-460c2b0ee764 "What do I need to open a Priority Banking Current Account")

* Sponsor's letter of no objection
* Salary Certificate (in case of salary transfer accounts). In the absence of a Salary Certificate, any one of the following documents may be provided:
+ Appointment letter/Contract copy
+ Pay slip (<3 months old)
+ Consolidated letter from HR for bulk accounts
+ Most recent statement of account if your salary is being transferred

As a result, we regularly re-evaluate and update this Privacy Policy. The date of the last revision of this Privacy Policy is set out at the end of the Privacy Policy and any changes made will take effect immediately upon posting to the ENBD Channels.  
If you have questions, comments, concerns or feedback regarding this Privacy Policy or any other privacy concern, please contact us at [**customercare@emiratesnbd.com**](mailto:customercare@emiratesnbd.com)  
It is not mandatory for you to provide Personal Information to us through ENBD Channels, but, if you choose not to do so, unfortunately, we will not be able to provide you with our services or respond to any queries you may have.  
Please note that as a user of ENBD Channels and our services, you are responsible for keeping your login information, including your login ID and password, confidential. If you believe that your login ID or password has been compromised or that someone else has accessed your account, please notify us immediately by contacting us at [**customercare@emiratesnbd.com**](mailto:customercare@emiratesnbd.com).  
This Privacy Policy is subject to ENBD General Terms and Conditions for accounts available at [**www.emiratesnbd.com**](https://www.emiratesnbd.com)  
**What kind of Personal Information do we collect?**

**What kind of Personal Information do we collect?**  
Depending on which ENBD Channels and services you use, we may collect different kinds of Personal Information from or about you.  
**Things you do and Personal Information you provide**  
We may collect Personal Information when you use our services and ENBD Channels, including when you sign up for an account, create or share, and message or communicate with others. This Personal Information may include your name, photo, address, email address, gender and date of birth and also Personal Information in or about the content you provide, such as the location of a photo or the date a file was created or any financial information. We may collect Personal Information about how you use ENBD Channels and our services, such as the types of content you view or engage with or the frequency and duration of your activities.  
**Things others do and Personal Information they provide**  
We may also collect Personal Information about you that other people provide when they use ENBD Channels or our services, such as when they share a photo of you, send a message to you, or upload, sync or import your contact details.  
**Your networks and connections**
title: Mobile Privacy Policy | Emirates NBD

text:
Mobile Privacy Policy | Emirates NBD > Privacy Policy

**Your networks and connections**  
We may also collect Personal Information about you and the people and groups you are connected to and how you interact with them, such as the people you communicate with the most or the groups you like to share with. We also collect contact Personal Information you provide if you upload, sync or import Personal Information (such as an address book) from a device.  
**Information about payments**  
If you use ENBD Channels or our services for purchases or financial transactions, we may collect Personal Information as a result of the purchase or transaction. This will include Personal Information such as your credit or debit card number, other credit or debit card related information, and other account and authentication related information, as well as billing, shipping and contact details.  
**Device Personal Information**  
We may collect Personal Information from or about the computers, phones, or other devices from where you use ENBD Channels or access our services, depending on the permissions you’ve granted. We may associate the Personal Information we collect from your different devices, which helps us provide consistent services across your devices and/or support security practices. Here are some examples of the device Personal Information we collect:  
* Attributes such as the operating system, hardware version, device settings, file and software names and types, battery and signal strength, and device identifiers.

* Device locations, including specific geographic locations, such as through GPS, Bluetooth, or WiFi signals
* Connection Personal Information such as the name of your mobile operator or ISP, browser type, language and time zone, mobile phone number and IP address.
* Information from websites and apps that use our services.  
We may also receive Personal Information about you and your activities from third-party partners, for example from a partner where we jointly offer services or from an advertiser about your experiences or interactions with them  
**ENBD affiliates**  
We may share your Personal Information with companies that are affiliates of ENBD or ENBD group companies or subcontractors in accordance with our and their terms and conditions, privacy policies and sharing your Personal Information is subject to ENBD General Terms and Conditions, as amended from time to time, which can be reviewed at www.emiratesnbd.com  
**Non-Personal Information**

**Non-Personal Information**  
We also collect information in a form that does not, on its own, permit direct association with any specific individual such as occupation, language, zip/area code, location, time zone, ip address etc. We may collect, use, transfer, and disclose non-personal information for any purpose. This information is aggregated and used to help us provide more useful information to our customers and to understand which of our services are of most interest. This aggregated data is considered non personal information for the purposes of this Privacy Policy.  
**How do we use your Personal Information?**  
We are passionate about creating engaging and customized experiences for our customers. We may use your Personal Information to help us provide better products and services. Here’s how:  
**Provide, improve and develop our services**  
We are able to create, develop, operate, deliver and improve our services, offer personalized content, and make suggestions for you by using your Personal Information to understand how you use and interact with our services and the people or things you’re connected to and interested in on and off ENBD Channels.  
When we have location Personal Information, we use it to tailor our services for you and others, like helping you to check-in and find local events or offers in your area.

We conduct surveys and research, test features in development, and analyze the Personal Information we have to evaluate and improve products and services, develop new products or features, and conduct audits and troubleshooting activities.  
**Communicate with you**  
We may use your Personal Information to send you marketing communications, communicate with you about our Services and let you know about our policies and terms. We also use your Personal Information to respond to you when you contact us. You can unsubscribe from emails at any time by clicking “unsubscribe” at the bottom of the email. You can also unsubscribe from mailing lists at any time by contacting us at [**customercare@emiratesnbd.com**](mailto:customercare@emiratesnbd.com).  
**Show and measure ads and services**  
We may use your Personal Information to improve our advertising and measurement systems so we can show you relevant ads and measure the effectiveness and reach of ads and services.  
**Online Session Information and Use is Collected to Improve Your Experience**  
The technical and navigational related Personal Information we collect, such as computer browser type, Internet protocol address, pages visited, and average time spent on ENBD Channels may be used, for example, to alert you to software compatibility issues, or it may be analyzed to improve the design and functionality of ENBD Channels and our services.

You will have the option to disable cookies. If you choose to do so, unfortunately, certain features of ENBD Channels will not be available once cookies are disabled.

We may also use third party service providers to help us analyze certain online activities. For example, these service providers may help us measure the performance of our online campaigns or analyze visitor activity. We may permit these service providers to use cookies and other technologies to perform these services for us.

**Where is your Personal Information Stored?**

## A financial powerhouse at your fingertips  
businessONLINE provides single access to all your banking accounts along with external account reporting  
* [Real-time information](#tab_bs72bbb8bf-5a3b-4808-8446-50d4857ed507 "Realtime information")
* [Higher customization](#tab_bs74b2b97d-59ac-4d56-83f9-22534ef56cfc "Higher customization")
* [Time-saving features](#tab_bsc30279ae-7fb8-43bc-a33b-288477ef3cf0 "Timesaving features")
* [Remote services](#tab_bsae55e746-bff1-413f-9f9c-cc40138edca4 "Remote services")
* [Customized Dashboard](#tab_bs975e489f-432b-46c4-ab15-21e3bb0cdcb9 "Customized Dashboard")  
#### Real-time information  
Have access to real-time aggregated cash positions across the bank and entities. Plus, get updates on your account status as well as account balances.  
![Real time information](/-/media/enbd/images/cib/account-management-and-reporting/real-time_1920x1080.png?la=en&h=1080&w=1920&hash=84DA3ECE244C2E0764B80E7DBD5A5914)  
#### Higher customization  
Download customized reports for reconciliation, planning, or forecasting online. Account statements can be downloaded in any format including MT940, CSV, PDF and Excel in a given date range along with the bank logo, allowing you to choose the format that best suits your requirements.  
![Higher customization](/-/media/enbd/images/cib/account-management-and-reporting/higher-customization_1920x1080.png?la=en&h=1080&w=1920&hash=320154579CB59CC9190D782D78395112)  
#### Time-saving features
title: Account Management and Reporting | Emirates NBD
section: A financial powerhouse at your fingertips

text:
Account Management and Reporting | Emirates NBD > A financial powerhouse at your fingertips

#### Time-saving features  
Download multi-account statements in a single click or update your trade license through the portal, reducing the time needed in doing these physically at bank branches or downloading multiple statements.  
![Time saving features](/-/media/enbd/images/cib/account-management-and-reporting/time-saving-features_1920x1080.png?la=en&h=1080&w=1920&hash=56C1E38D6547A1205A66CFABDA77DEB7)  
#### Remote services  
Effortlessly provide instructions to the bank from the comfort of your office premise to manage task-based requests. Monitor requests online and enjoy faster turnaround time, complete transaction visibility, and reporting capabilities through two methods:  
* Online Drop Box – Upload signed instructions or forms for the bank to process
* Online Form\* - Enter the details online for transactions already initiated from businessONLINE.  
\*applicable for online TT amendment, TT Recall, Token Request  
![Remote services](/-/media/enbd/images/cib/account-management-and-reporting/remote-services_1920x1080.png?la=en&h=1080&w=1920&hash=FBB7D80B16E2F938F8B4EF8B4BF8A137)  
#### Customized Dashboard

#### Customized Dashboard  
Access widget-based customised dashboards for various aspects of your business to track, monitor, and share your critical metrics. For example, the CXO Dashboard is an executive dashboard for the CEOs, CFOs and Corporate Treasurers of our corporate clients to provide a consolidated view of your financial position with the bank including assets and liabilities, accounts summary, FX positions, facility utilization, and both market-data exchange rates and benchmark interest rates.

## Why open a current account online in the UAE?  
The practical case for opening a current account online is straightforward. A branch visit typically takes 60 to 90 minutes once you factor in travel, queuing, and paperwork. An online application takes about 5 minutes to complete, and you can do it on a Sunday evening or during a lunch break.  
Beyond the time saving, digital account opening gives you access from day one. Emirates NBD's 24/7 Mobile and Online Banking lets you check balances, transfer funds and pay bills the moment your account is live.  
The UAE Central Bank has also announced an e-KYC platform initiative to streamline digital onboarding across banks. While the platform is still being rolled out, it signals a move toward faster and more standardised account opening in the future.  
Here is what online opening gives you that a branch visit typically does not:  
* No queuing, no travel time
* Applications accepted around the clock, every day of the year
* Document uploads from your phone gallery
* Instant or near-instant confirmation of receipt
* Access to multi-currency accounts and salary features from day one

Open Current Account Online UAE – Quick guide | Emirates NBD > Eligibility and documents for online current account opening

## Eligibility and documents for online current account opening  
Emirates NBD's current accounts are open to individual UAE resident customers, both salaried and non-salaried.  
Most UAE banks ask for:  
* UAE residency status (a valid residence visa)
* Age of 18 or above
* A monthly income that meets the bank's minimum threshold (Emirates NBD's Personal Banking Classic package carries no minimum salary requirement, making it a practical starting point if your income is below 5,000. However, the Plus and Plus Maximizer packages require a minimum salary of 5,000.)
* A UAE mobile number for OTP verification  
If you're self-employed or non-salaried, you can substitute a trade licence or a three-month bank statement in place of a salary certificate.  
The core documents you'll need are:  
* Valid passport (original and a clear copy)
* UAE residence visa page
* Original Emirates ID
* Salary certificate dated within the last three months (or a trade licence/bank statement for non-salaried applicants)
* Proof of address, such as a tenancy contract or recent utility bill  
When preparing your digital scans, use PDF or JPEG format and keep each file under 5 MB. Photograph documents on a flat, well-lit surface to avoid rejected uploads. You can find the full document checklist on the [Emirates NBD Help and Support](/en/help-and-support/documents-to-open-an-account)page.

The process of opening a current account is faster than most people expect. Before you start, have your documents scanned and ready on your phone or laptop. Visit the [Emirates NBD account opening](/en/campaigns/open-account)page and complete the online form. Enter your personal details, contact information, and employment or salary data. Scanning your Emirates ID at this stage auto-populates many fields, saving time.  
##### Step 3: Upload your required documents  
Attach your passport copy, residence visa page, Emirates ID, salary certificate and proof of address. Use PDF or JPEG files, keep them under 5 MB each and photograph them in good light. All uploads are secured via bank-grade encryption aligned with CBUAE data protection standards.

## Online banking safety and security tips  
Opening your account online is safe, provided you follow a few best practices:  
* Use a strong, unique password for your online banking login and change it periodically
* Never share your PIN, OTP or online banking credentials with anyone
* Always use a secure, private Wi-Fi connection when accessing your banking app
* Keep your ENBD X app updated so you have the latest security patches
* Be alert to phishing messages, Emirates NBD will never ask for your password by email or SMS
* Keep your debit card and cheque book secure at all times to prevent misuse  
If you ever suspect unauthorised activity on your account, contact Emirates NBD immediately. Bank-grade encryption protects your data during every online transaction, and CBUAE regulations require your personal information to remain stored within the UAE.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)  
[How long does approval take after I submit documents?](#faqs-what-is-an-itm "What is an ITM")  
Approval timelines vary depending on the completion of your documents and verification steps. If your documents are clear and fully uploaded, it should take no more than one to two business days. Check the Emirates NBD application page for the latest guidance on processing times.  
[Can non-residents open a UAE current account online?](#faqs-what-is-the-maximum-amount-for-a-transaction-via-itm "Whats the maximum amount for a transaction via ITM")  
Current accounts in the UAE generally require a valid UAE residence visa and an Emirates ID. Non-residents are typically limited to savings accounts, and some banks apply higher minimum balances for non-resident arrangements. If you've recently arrived in the UAE, securing your Emirates ID is the practical first step.  
[What if my salary is below 5,000?](#faqs-do-you-require-any-documents-from-customer-for-performing-transactions-over-itm "Do you require any documents from customer for performing transactions over ITM")  
You can still open a current account. Emirates NBD's Personal Banking Classic package carries no minimum salary requirement. You'll need to maintain a minimum average monthly balance of 3,000, and a fall-below fee of 26.25 per month applies if the balance drops below that threshold.

##  
A bond is a debt security issued by a government/corporation or any other entity to raise funds. It is a contract to repay borrowed money with interest at fixed dates (it is like a loan where the issuer is the borrower, and the holder is the lender). Bonds are not capital protected, and you can lose your money.  
##  
Sukuk is a form of Shari'ah-compliant fixed-income capital markets instruments that represent an interest in an underlying funding arrangement structured according to Islamic finance norms. Investment Sukuk are certificates of equal value representing undivided shares in ownership of tangible assets, usufruct, and services or (in the ownership of) the assets of particular projects or special investment activity,  
##  
Bonds are issued to fund day-to-day operations or to finance specific goals. When you buy a bond, you are lending your money for a certain period of time to the issuer. In exchange, the borrower promises to pay you interest every year and to return your principal at ‘maturity’, when the loan comes due, or at ‘call’ if the bond is of the type that can be called earlier than its maturity (more on this later). The length of time to maturity is called the ‘term’.  
##  
A bond’s notional value, is known as its ‘par value’ which is typically 100. Its interest payment is known as its ‘coupon’.

The clean price refers to the bond’s price excluding accrued interest. In contrast, the dirty price includes both the clean price and the accrued interest.  
##  
Bond ratings indicate the creditworthiness of a bond and its issuer. They help investors evaluate the associated risk: the higher the rating, the lower the risk, and vice versa. Ratings from AAA to BBB- are classified as investment grade, while those below BBB- are categorized as high-yield bonds. These ratings are typically assigned by three independent agencies: S&P, Moody’s, and Fitch.  
##  
Payment rank in bonds refers to the order of priority in which bondholders are paid if the issuer faces financial distress or defaults. Bonds with a higher rank, such as secured or senior bonds, are paid before lower-ranked bonds, like subordinated or junior subordinated bonds.  
##  
Like any other investment product, this product is linked to market performance hence it is not capital-guaranteed and will be associated with some risks. These risks include and are not limited to investment risks, issuer risk/default risk, interest rate risk, market risk, sale prior to maturity, lack of liquidity and secondary market trading, currency risk and embedded options. ### Disclaimer  
#### The main risk factors are summarized below for your information  
You should understand the nature of the risks associated with each and every circumstance outlined below and should obtain relevant and specific professional advice before making any decision. The list below does not, however, claim to be a complete list of all related risks. You should assume all risk associated with any decision you make and you shall have no right against Emirates NBD in connection with such decision.  
#### Risk / default risk  
The value of the security may decline for a number of reasons which directly relate to the issuer, including, but not limited to, the issuer’s credit worthiness. In addition, there is a risk that the Security Issuer will be unable to pay the contractual interest on the security and/or its principal, in a timely manner, or at all. Emirates NBD does not guarantee or warrant any obligations of the Security Issuer to pay the principal amount of the security, or any contractual interests accrued thereon.  
#### Interest rate risk

text:

#### Interest rate risk  
Market interest rates are a function of several factors such as the demand for, and supply of, money in the economy, the inflation rate, the stage that the business cycle is in, as well as the government's monetary and fiscal policies. Should the market interest rate rise from the date of the security’s purchase, the security’s price will fall accordingly. The security will then trade at a discount to the purchase price.  
#### Market risk  
Market movement, which can be influenced by many factors, including, but not limited to, issuer risk, interest rate risk, market sentiment and changes in economic, financial or political environments may result in the fluctuation of prices. Market risk results from the unpredictability of market movements and is inherent in any investment; such risk may cause the value of the investment to fall rapidly, as well as rise, and you may not get back the amount originally invested.  
#### Sale prior to maturity  
Where a security is capital protected, the stated level of capital protection only applies at maturity. The sale of the security prior to the stated maturity date may result in you receiving an amount less than that originally invested at inception. The sale price would be a function of fees, and prevailing market conditions.  
#### Lack of liquidity and secondary market trading

#### Lack of liquidity and secondary market trading  
Lack of liquidity may result in difficulty finding a price to sell an investment you have made. In the case of company bankruptcy, suspension of trading, takeover rumors, or flights of capital from a country in crisis, this may mean it is impossible to find any price to close out your position. This could lead to substantial losses up to the value of the investment. No assurance can be given that any trading market for the securities will exist or whether any such market will be liquid or illiquid. If the Securities are not traded on any exchange, pricing information may be more difficult to obtain, and the liquidity and price of the Securities may be adversely affected.  
#### Currency risk

#### Currency risk  
Changes in exchange rates between currencies or the conversion from one currency to another may cause the value of the investment to diminish or increase. Currency exchange rates may fluctuate significantly over short periods of time. Earnings on investment in foreign currencies are dependent on the prevailing foreign exchange rates. Adverse exchange rate movements may erase interest earnings completely or cause a loss of principal relative to your home currency. Investments in assets denominated in a foreign currency are subject to the risk of movements in that currency's exchange rate. The exchange-rate risk on investments in foreign-currency denominated assets applies not only to investments returnable in these foreign currencies, but also to the assets denominated in the foreign currencies and traded in the domestic currency, since their price development usually tracks changes in the exchange rate of the currency in which they are denominated.  
#### Embedded options

#### Embedded options  
The investment may comprise embedded options such as a callable option, a cap on the coupon of a floating rate bond, an option to switch fixed to floating coupon and vice versa, etc. Please refer to the Issuer’s Prospectus for details. Action by the issuer on the back of an embedded option will impact your expected pay-off from the investment. For example, a Callable Bond has call provisions, which allows the bond issuer to buy back the bond from the bondholders and retire the issue at a predetermined price. This is usually done when interest rates have fallen substantially since the issue date. Call provisions allow the issuer to retire the old high coupon bonds in a bid to lower debt costs. Under these circumstances you will be forced to give up a high yielding security, with an adverse effect on the anticipated return.

## Fees & charges  
If you're opening a Skywards Savings Account, a one-time joining fee of 2,500 will apply. From the 2nd year onwards, there will be a monthly fee of 250.  
There are no fees to open any other account with us.  
If you’re not holding a payroll account with us, or if you're holding a Company Account, you’ll be required to maintain a minimum average monthly balance based on your banking package. Please note, for every month that this balance is not maintained, you may be charged a fee.

## Quick Answers  
[I’ve not received my OTP. What should I do?](#accordion-1fdbbdfb-f81a-443c-9711-d247d51d6222 "Ive not received my OTP. What should I do")  
Please ensure you’re using a mobile number registered with us. If you still don’t receive the OTP SMS and OTP Email, call us on [**+971 600 54 0000**](tel:+971600540000) and when prompted, say ‘Authentication Code not received’.  
[Is it safe to share my card number?](#accordion-c14e16bd-40cc-461b-87a6-b5f8a7f4570b "Is it safe to share my card number")  
You should avoid sharing any of your bank details with people you don’t know or can’t trust. It’s ok to share this information with the bank in a safe manner. ## Enjoy the rewards  
* **Dollar cost averaging:** Since you invest fixed sums at regular intervals, you pick up more units when the prices are low and less units when the prices are high. There is no need to time the markets as you invest at regular intervals.  
* **Hedge against inflation:** Experts agree that investing in capital market securities is a better hedge against inflation compared to just holding cash.  
* **Compounding:** Earnings are re-invested to generate additional returns.  
* **Easy withdrawal:** Freedom to withdraw partially or exit with no charges.

**Tim Mason** is Managing Director and Head of Innovation at Deutsche Bank, where he leads the bank’s global AI program and enterprise-wide transformation efforts. With over 25 years of experience across banking, consulting, and tech strategy, he has played a key role in integrating generative AI across the organization to drive efficiency and innovation.  
Tim has held several leadership roles since joining Deutsche Bank in 2010 and currently oversees the bank’s AI initiative, “Indra.” He previously worked with PA Consulting and led his own consultancy. He holds an MBA from Henley Management College and a degree in Industrial Design from Brunel University.  
**Daniele Magazzeni** is the Chief Analytics Officer for the Commercial & Investment Bank at JP MorganChase, responsible for integrating advanced analytics and AI into business strategies. He focuses on advancing AI capabilities, reusing solutions across lines of business, fostering a culture of innovation, and ensuring regulatory compliance. Additionally, as the EMEA CAO, he accelerates analytics adoption and fosters innovation in Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, while engaging with regional stakeholders, regulators, and clients.

He implemented initiatives around Customer Experience, Generative AI, and Customer acquisition platforms. With a strong foundation in cloud architecture and LLMs, Bruno has built and scaled global tech capabilities that support over a million customers across Latin America in the banking,e-commerce, and retail industries.  
Before Nubank, Bruno held leadership roles at CI&T where he spearheaded digital transformation projects for major brands such as Carrefour, Netshoes, and Nestlé. He is passionate about building event-driven, scalable systems and exploring cutting-edge technologies.

## FAQs  
[What does ‘Points adjustments’ on Online Banking and Mobile Banking mean?](#faqs-what-does-points-adjustments-on-online-banking-and-mobile-banking-mean "What does Points adjustments on Online Banking and Mobile Banking mean")  
Points adjustments reflect changes to your rewards balance because of deductions or additional rewards earned. Deductions can happen when rewards you earned for a particular transaction are no longer valid due to a refund or conversion into a 0% installment plan. Additional rewards can be credited to you during a promotion.

text:
Foreign Currency Current Account in the UAE | Emirates NBD > Requirements and documents for opening an account

## Requirements and documents for opening an account  
[UAE Nationals](#accordion-1fd07131-194a-4e8b-923c-a60817f737c8 "UAE Nationals")  
* **Identification**
+ Original Emirates ID and copy
+ Copy of passport
* **In case of a salary transfer account, we’ll need one of the following documents:**
+ Copy of Labor Card
+ Copy of Employee ID
+ Latest salary letter  
[Expats](#accordion-26da4fe4-c636-4034-9805-761af5a37218 "Expats")  
* **Identification**
+ Original Emirates ID and copy
+ Copy of passport
* **In case of a salary transfer account, we’ll need one of the following documents:**
+ Salary transfer letter (not more than 30 days from date of issue for non-government companies. For government companies, validity as mentioned in the letter.)
+ Copy of appointment letter or contract
+ Copy of pay slip (less than a month old)
+ Statement with previous month’s salary
+ **For bulk accounts:** consolidated letter from HR (with salary of each employee mentioned)
* **Additional documents**
+ In some cases, additional documents may be requested in order to proceed with opening an account  
[Non-residents](#accordion-1dc160e3-cd1d-4c5a-a878-0b297fb2874a "Nonresidents")  
* **Passport and copy with visa page and one of the following documents:**
+ Utility bill (not more than 3 months old)
+ Bank statements (not more than 3 months old, you can print these off Online Banking too)

text:
Foreign Currency Current Account in the UAE | Emirates NBD > Requirements and documents for opening an account

+ Utility bill (not more than 3 months old)
+ Bank statements (not more than 3 months old, you can print these off Online Banking too)
+ Reference letter from a banker in home country confirming the length and nature of your relationship with them (this should be a minimum of 12 months); residential address as per the home country bank records  
[GCC Nationals](#accordion-883bd762-40e5-4d5c-adff-56be5954e32d "GCC Nationals")  
* **Identification**
+ Passport and copy or UAE National ID and copy
* **For current or checking accounts any one of the following documents:**
+ UAE National ID
+ Labour Card and copy
+ Work Permit and copy
+ Letter from employer
+ Copy of recent telephone or electricity bill (not more than 3 months old)
+ Tenancy contract in your name  
[Self-employed (non-individuals)](#accordion-799cf70a-1e13-4239-9f12-a9c5bf8108cd "Selfemployed nonindividuals")  
* Passport and Emirates ID copies of all signatories/owners/directors
* Trade license if the company is in the UAE
* Memorandum of association (MOA)
* Board resolution

# How to set realistic financial goals for yourself  
![](https://cdn.emiratesnbd.com/assets/images/logomark.svg)  
Curated by Emirates NBD  
2 min read  
![](https://cdn.emiratesnbd.com/assets/images/calendar.svg)  
24/06/2025  
![](https://cdn.emiratesnbd.com/assets/images/show.svg)  
49,129  
![](https://cdn.emiratesnbd.com/assets/images/share.svg)  
Share  
![](https://cdn.emiratesnbd.com/deals/images/tiles/How-to-diversify-portfolio.jpg)  
Let's be honest – many of us struggle with saving money. Things come up, life happens and unexpected expenses can dwindle our bank balances alarmingly quickly. Setting financial goals that are achievable can help provide structure and accountability. Basing your financial goals on your current behaviours and tendencies is key to setting realistic targets.  
**Understand your saving habits**  
Before setting any financial goals, take some time to objectivelyanalysehow you currently manage money day-to-day. Look at the past 3 to 6 months of spending and saving activity. What do you notice? Do you tend to spend most of your money every month with little left over? Do you have trouble resisting impulse purchases?
title: How to set realistic financial goals for yourself | Emirates NBD
section: How to set realistic financial goals for yourself

text:
How to set realistic financial goals for yourself | Emirates NBD > How to set realistic financial goals for yourself

Try to understand your usual behaviours around spending, saving and financial decision making. Then, identify what is behind those behaviours. For example, you may be overspending when stressed, or find it hard to deny "little luxuries" after a long week at work. The more insight you can get into what drives your financial habits, good and bad, the better equipped you'll be to set appropriate goals.  
**Start small with your goals**  
Armed with this self-knowledge, begin crafting S.M.A.R.T. financial goals – ones that are **S**pecific, **M**easurable, **A**chievable, **R**elevant, and **T**ime-bound. But make sure to start small and focus on incremental change that is easy to sustain.  
For instance, if your analysis shows you have trouble saving consistently, set a goal to automatically transfer just 50 every week to savings. Or, if you know you overspend on convenience items, commit to limiting takeout meals to just one day a week.  
Baby steps are best when trying to change behaviours. Don't expect perfection right away. Setting goals that stretch your comfort zone too quickly, often fails.  
**Automate what you can**  
Speaking of stretching comfort zones, automating your finances can work wonders. Setting up automatic transfers into separate savings accounts or automatically investing a set amount from each paycheck takes the decision-making out of your hands so you don’t really have to think about it.
title: How to set realistic financial goals for yourself | Emirates NBD
section: How to set realistic financial goals for yourself

text:
How to set realistic financial goals for yourself | Emirates NBD > How to set realistic financial goals for yourself

Once you automate something like a recurring transfer into an emergency fund, maintaining that positive financial habit becomes effortless. The passive nature of automation may help sidestep common self-control issues that often sabotage sound money management practices.  
**Give every dirham a job**  
Budgeting can transform scattered intuitions about where your money goes every month, into cold, hard facts. Once armed with accurate spending data, you can strategically assign your money in accordance with your priorities. Budgeting experts recommendcategorisingexpenses as either needs, wants, savings and/or debt payments.  
Be brutally honest about available income after your essential needs are covered. What can realistically go toward savings goals or extra debt payments? This clear breakdown reduces guesswork and wishful thinking about finances. Now your dirhams have specific jobs aligned with your values, which relates to your smart goal setting.  
**Assess progress frequently**  
The final piece of the goal-setting puzzle is consistent tracking and assessment. Don't just set well-intentioned goals then forget about them! Try setting calendar reminders to check in on your progress throughout the month.  
Are automated transfers occurring regularly? Have impulse purchases decreased? How much progress have you made towards paying off credit card debt? Frequent accountability checks reinforce motivation and highlight problem spots.
title: How to set realistic financial goals for yourself | Emirates NBD
section: How to set realistic financial goals for yourself

text:
How to set realistic financial goals for yourself | Emirates NBD > How to set realistic financial goals for yourself

If certain goals need adjustment, that's okay. Revaluate what's realistic with the insight gained, and tweak goals or timelines accordingly. The key is consistency and continued awareness. Progress may not be linear, but as long you pay attention and remain committed, you're on the right path.

text:
Open a Minor Account | Support | Emirates NBD > Visit our branch

## Visit our branch  
Encourage your children below the age of 18 to manage their savings and spending money by opening a Minor Account for them.  
To open a Minor Account, the child’s guardian must visit [one of our branches](/en/branches-and-atms)with these documents:  
* the guardian’s Emirates ID or passport
* the minor’s Emirates ID or passport
* a court order if the father or grandfather is not the guardian  
The account will be opened immediately, and a debit card will be issued in the name of the guardian or minor, as you desire.
title: Open a Minor Account | Support | Emirates NBD

text:
Open a Minor Account | Support | Emirates NBD > FAQs

## FAQs  
[Is there an alternative to opening a Minor Account?](#faqs-is-there-an-alternative-to-opening-a-minor-account "Is there an alternative to opening a Minor Account")  
Yes, you can open an [EarlySaver Account](/en/accounts/savings-accounts/earlysaver-account)which is a savings account under your own banking profile. This account offers attractive interest rates and can be linked to a top-up deposit. The account can be instantly opened under the name of the child, and you can have a supplementary debit card issued to the child as well.  
[How can I convert my Minor Account to a standard individual account?](#faqs-how-can-i-convert-my-minor-account-to-a-standard-individual-account "How can I convert my Minor Account to a standard individual account")  
Individuals, ages 18 and above, can convert their Minor Account to a standard individual account by visiting the nearest[Emirates NBD branch](/en/branches-and-atms)along with their passport or Emirates ID for identification.  
[What's the minimum age for a minor account?](#faqs-whats-the-minimum-age-for-a-minor-account "Whats the minimum age for a minor account")  
There is no minimum age requirement to open a minor account.  
[Is there a minimum amount a minor account should be opened with?](#faqs-is-there-a-minimum-amount-a-minor-account-should-be-opened-with "Is there a minimum amount a minor account should be opened with")  
There is no minimum balance or deposit required to open a minor account.

# Convert your fee payment into 0% installments up to 24 months on your Credit Card  
This academic year, convert education fees into easy payment plans with your Emirates NBD Credit Card.  
#### Pay Education Fees  
Pay school fees more than 1,000  
#### 0% Installment Plan  
Convert your fee payment into easy installments up to 24 months on your Credit Card

#### Redeem your Plus Points  
**What steps should I carry out to redeem my Plus Points for education fee payments?**  
* **Step 1:** You have to pay your education fees in full using your Credit Card to your respective school or university.
* **Step 2:** Once the payment is processed on your Card, you can [**Click here**](/en/help-and-support/redeeming-plus-points) to request Plus Points redemption to offset the partial or complete education fee amount.
* **Step 3:** Once your redemption request is processed, you will be notified via SMS and the amount offset by your Plus Points will reflect on your Credit Card statement.  
**Did you know that you can find out your Plus Points balance instantly?**  
* Simply SMS
"REWARDS last 4 digits of your card number " to 4455  
How Plus Points redemption is calculated:  
**1 Plus Point** is equivalent to **1** for redemption against Education Fees

## UAE Direct Debit System  
The UAE Direct Debit System (UAEDDS) allows customers to set up automatic payments for their Emirates NBD loan using an operative account held with another bank in the UAE.  
You can set up Direct Debit Authorization (DDA) for your loans using:  
* A physical DDA form
* A DDA form via UAE PASS

If your loan is with another bank, initiate a request through the bank where the operative account is held. The relevant bank will then forward the Direct Debit Authorization to Emirates NBD.

section: Setting up a UAE Direct Debit

text:
Direct debit for loans | Support | Emirates NBD > UAE Direct Debit options

## UAE Direct Debit options  
**Fixed payment**  
For the Fixed Amount option, the agreed EMI amount with the Bank will be debited from your account on each due date, as per the Direct Debit Authorization (DDA). The customer may, where applicable, define minimum and/or maximum limits for the debit amount in accordance with the agreed mandate.  
**Variable amount**  
For the Variable Amount option, the amount debited may vary. The customer may define a minimum and/or maximum limit (“cap”) for each debit under the Direct Debit Authorization. If you decide not to agree a cap, the creditor is authorised to determine the amount to be debited from the customer’s account. The paying bank shall not be held liable for any disputes between the customer and the creditor in relation to the debited amount, except in cases where the agreed cap if any, has been breached.
title: Direct debit for loans | Support | Emirates NBD

text:
Direct debit for loans | Support | Emirates NBD > Cancelling a request

## Cancelling a request  
You will need to submit a written request to the lending bank to cancel your direct debit facility. The cancellation may take up to 5 working days.  
For loans with Emirates NBD, DDS cancellation is automated for matured loans. In case of changes to repayment accounts, the old DDS is cancelled by the Bank prior to the new DDS account being set up.

## FAQs  
[Is there a forum where I can raise complaint related to direct debit?](#faqs-is-there-a-forum-where-i-can-raise-a-complaint-related-to-direct-debit "Is there a forum where I can raise complaint related to direct debit")  
You should contact the originator to raise any complaints related to direct debits. If you wish to raise a dispute regarding a direct debit transaction, please visit[**http://www.centralbank.ae**](http://www.centralbank.ae/)for more information.  
[Will my account details for direct debit be shared or made available to a third party?](#faqs-will-my-account-details-for-direct-debit-be-shared-or-made-available-to-a-third-party "Will my account details for direct debit be shared or made available to a third party")  
The details of your direct debit will not be shared with a third party without the written consent of the Central Bank of the UAE.  
[Will lenders and bankers have access to my personal information when I set up direct debit?](#faqs-will-lenders-and-bankers-have-access-to-my-personal-information-when-i-set-up-a-direct-debit "Will lenders and bankers have access to my personal information when I set up direct debit")  
Lenders and bankers will have access only to the details that you will provide in the Direct Debit Authority form for the specific Direct Debit Authority that has been requested to be set up.
title: Direct debit for loans | Support | Emirates NBD

text:
Direct debit for loans | Support | Emirates NBD > FAQs

[Can I decline the direct debit option and opt to pay only by post-dated cheque (PDC)?](#faqs-can-i-decline-the-direct-debit-option-and-opt-for-paying-only-by-postdated "Can I decline the direct debit option and opt to pay only by postdated cheque PDC")  
No, all payments can only be made using direct debit. Landing institutions should not accept post-dated cheques. If any institution demands that you pay using a PDC, then you should immediately report it to the Central Bank of the UAE. Please visit[**http://www.centralbank.ae**](http://www.centralbank.ae/)for more information.

text:
Installment Payment Plan (IPP) Cancellation Request | Emirates NBD > Quick Answers

## Quick Answers  
[Can I cancel my Installment Payment Plan (IPP) if my card is blocked?](#accordion-4e1a2990-eade-4c18-a84b-3f1ce83593b4 "Can I cancel my Installment Payment Plan IPP if my card is blocked")  
Yes, you can. IPP cancellation can be done for active and blocked cards. The total amount will be reflected as an outstanding on your credit card statement even if your card is blocked.  
[How much does it cost to cancel my installment plan?](#accordion-180c511c-d903-4f53-a254-941c0048492a "How much does it cost to cancel my installment plan")  
To cancel IPP, you will have to settle the remaining principal outstanding plus the foreclosure fee. The foreclosure fee is 1.05% of principal outstanding plus 5% VAT.  
[I want to follow up on a previous request.](#accordion-9cc42ac7-6e1c-4465-a67d-a22ca8794488 "I want to follow up on a previous request.")  
You can track your previous request by calling us on [**+971 600 54 0000**](tel:+971600540000) and when prompted, say ‘follow up on my request’.  
[Can I cancel my Installment Payment Plan (IPP) if my card is blocked?](#accordion-4e1a2990-eade-4c18-a84b-3f1ce83593b4 "Can I cancel my Installment Payment Plan IPP if my card is blocked")  
Yes, you can. IPP cancellation can be done for active and blocked cards. The total amount will be reflected as an outstanding on your credit card statement even if your card is blocked.

## Requirements and documents for opening an account  
[UAE Nationals](#accordion-e594ce0c-d7ab-4c50-b0aa-8203ccc4eb8e "UAE Nationals")  
* **Identification**
+ Original Emirates ID and copy
+ Copy of passport
* **In case of a salary transfer account, we’ll need one of the following documents:**
+ Copy of Labour card
+ Copy of Employee ID
+ Latest salary letter
+ Copy of employment visa page from passport  
[Expats](#accordion-77cf7b8c-76dd-47b4-8124-c9e8ce8ba793 "Expats")  
* **Identification**
+ Original Emirates ID and copy
+ Copy of passport
* **In case of a salary transfer account, we’ll need one of the following documents:**
+ Salary transfer letter (not more than 30 days from date of issue for non-government companies. For government companies, validity as mentioned in the letter.)
+ Copy of appointment letter or contract
+ Copy of payslip (less than months old)
+ Statement with previous month’s salary
+ **For bulk accounts:** consolidated letter from HR (with salary of each employee mentioned)  
[Non-residents](#accordion-faf7f0de-e414-4c46-a2ab-74e2c9f18b17 "Nonresidents")  
* **Passport and copy with visa page and one of the following documents**
+ Utility bill (not more than 3 months old)
+ Bank statements (not more than 3 months old and you can print these off online banking too)

## Business Continuity Management  
Our business continuity approach helps us maintain critical banking services and support our customers during unexpected disruptions.
title: Business continuity plan | Emirates NBD

text:
Business continuity plan | Emirates NBD > Our commitment to continuity

### Our commitment to continuity  
The Bank has established a comprehensive business continuity framework to support ongoing resilience and the continued delivery of critical services during emergencies, disasters, or major disruptions. This framework is designed to minimise operational impact, protect customers, employees, and stakeholders, and support the timely restoration of essential services across a wide range of disruption scenarios.
title: Business continuity plan | Emirates NBD

text:
Business continuity plan | Emirates NBD > Strong governance and oversight

### Strong governance and oversight  
Our business continuity arrangements are aligned with relevant regulatory and supervisory requirements and operate within a defined governance structure. Senior management provides active oversight, with clear roles and responsibilities in place for crisis management, emergency response, business recovery, and technology recovery. This helps support accountability and coordinated action when it is needed most.
title: Business continuity plan | Emirates NBD

text:
Business continuity plan | Emirates NBD > Resilient operating arrangements

### Resilient operating arrangements  
To support continuity when primary facilities are unavailable or affected, the Group has implemented alternative operating arrangements. These include geographically dispersed locations and flexible working capabilities that help maintain agility and adaptability during disruptions. Multiple customer service and communication channels are also maintained to support continued access to essential services.
title: Business continuity plan | Emirates NBD

text:
Business continuity plan | Emirates NBD > Recovery and readiness

### Recovery and readiness  
Disaster recovery capabilities are maintained to restore critical systems and data in line with established recovery objectives, while recognising that certain external factors may affect outcomes. Business continuity and disaster recovery plans are regularly reviewed, updated, and tested through drills, simulations, and scenario-based exercises to assess readiness and effectiveness.
title: Business continuity plan | Emirates NBD

text:
Business continuity plan | Emirates NBD > Continuous improvement

### Continuous improvement  
Through strong governance, regular testing, and ongoing enhancement, the Bank remains committed to maintaining business continuity arrangements that are robust, proportionate, and effective. This helps support continued operations even under challenging conditions.

text:
Business continuity plan | Emirates NBD

##  
We have a comprehensive business continuity plan in place to ensure the uninterrupted delivery of essential banking services. This includes maintaining critical infrastructure, diversifying our operational centres and prioritising the safety of our staff to keep our systems running. We are monitoring the situation and adapting our operations to ensure we can support our customers and maintain the stability of the financial services you rely on every day.  
##  
If you can’t get through to us using Phone Banking or WhatsApp, it may be due to temporary disruptions or high volumes of calls and messages. Rest assured our staff are working round the clock to resolve any issues.  
For immediate and urgent issues, such as reporting a lost or stolen card, you can often manage this instantly and securely through the [**ENBD X**](/en/ways-of-banking/mobile-banking) app or [**Online Banking**](/en/ways-of-banking/online-banking).  
##  
Unverified information can create unnecessary concern. We encourage you to rely only on official Emirates NBD channels, including our website, the [**ENBD X**](/en/ways-of-banking/mobile-banking) app, verified social media accounts and direct bank communications. If information hasn’t come from an official bank source, please exercise caution before acting on it.  
##
title: Business continuity plan | Emirates NBD

text:
Business continuity plan | Emirates NBD

##  
Digital banking continues to offer a secure, reliable and convenient way to manage finances without the need to handle large amounts of cash. We encourage you to continue using our trusted digital channels for day-to-day banking.  
##  
The situation is being monitored continuously by our management and operational teams. Any updates that impact customers will be communicated immediately through our official channels.  
##  
To stay informed of the most accurate and up to date information, please check the [**Emirates NBD**](https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en) website, [**ENBD X**](/en/ways-of-banking/mobile-banking) app notifications, and official bank emails and social media channels.  
##  
If a digital channel is temporarily slow, please allow it some time. Networks can be unstable during this time. If you need support, you can call our customer support team on [**+971 600 540000**](tel:+971600540000).  
##  
Our [**ATMs**](/en/branches-and-atms) and digital transfers remain your best options for urgent access to cash. If you’re unable to access a preferred channel due to local disruptions, please check for the nearest available service points on our website. If you need support, please call [**+971 600 540000**](tel:+971600540000).

# The latte factor: How small daily expenses add up over time  
![](https://cdn.emiratesnbd.com/assets/images/logomark.svg)  
Curated by Emirates NBD  
2 min read  
![](https://cdn.emiratesnbd.com/assets/images/calendar.svg)

![](https://cdn.emiratesnbd.com/assets/images/share.svg)

![](https://cdn.emiratesnbd.com/deals/images/tiles/emirati_man_look.jpg)  
Explore how everyday indulgences like coffee, eating out, or small purchases can impact long-term financial health.  
It’s very easy to live-in-the-moment and indulge your ‘wants’ over your ‘needs’ as if to compensate for the stress and toil of modern-day living. And before you know it, that little frothy pick-me-up latte on your way to work or that guilty e-commerce binge, has added up to a substantial sum by the end of the month.  
**Identifying unnecessary expenses**  
Whether you have a super tight budget to balance through the year or have factored in a generous allowance to tide you through a rough time at work, often it’s these seemingly insignificant daily indulgences that waylay your finances. Sure, that weekly night out is great and that pizza takeaway is nice, but at what cost?
title: How small daily expenses add up over time | Emirates NBD
section: The latte factor: How small daily expenses add up over time

text:
How small daily expenses add up over time | Emirates NBD > The latte factor: How small daily expenses add up over time

The digital ease of paying for indulgences with a tap of your card or a click on your favourite shopping sites, makes it tough to keep track of your purchase history. But if you want to keep a check on impulsive buys and unnecessary expenses, you need to start by reviewing your spending patterns to understand where your money is going, every single day. Here are some ways to do this:  
* **Budgeting apps:** Mobile apps that connect with your financial account enable you to track and categorise expenses on a daily basis. Choose one that you like and keep a close tab on where your Dirhams are going.
* **Allocate a ‘Live for the moment’ budget:** Because we are human after all! Put a specific amount into this budget after studying your regular monthly expenses for a few months. This ensures that things like an expected supermarket dash, tips to service providers or that fast-food craving in the middle of the week are all catered for.
* **Plan in advance:** Research showcases that food delivery apps and takeaways are the biggest culprits when it comes to upending people’s carefully set out monthly budgets. This might seem simple, but the basic task of pre planning your weekly meals, so you know exactly what you’re having for dinner on a Wednesday, can avoid that sudden splurge mid-week when you might be tempted to order in.  
**Treat yourself when you reach your goals**
title: How small daily expenses add up over time | Emirates NBD
section: The latte factor: How small daily expenses add up over time

text:
How small daily expenses add up over time | Emirates NBD > The latte factor: How small daily expenses add up over time

**Treat yourself when you reach your goals**  
Unless you are aware of exactly where that 5 is going each morning you will have no clue where 5,000 has gone by the end of the year. By saving yourself from spending on frivolous stuff, you can actually end up with more money to spend on something valuable for yourself. It could be that designer bag you thought was out of your budget or a new class you want to enroll in to upskill yourself.  
The treat could be a bigger ‘Live for the moment’ budget for the next month enabling you to indulge in what is truly priceless – yourself.

# GCC Family Offices Must Adapt, Manage Complex Needs To Succeed  
14 June 2023  
[Share](javascript:void(0); "Share")  
![GCC Family Offices Must Adapt, Manage Complex Needs To Succeed](/-/media/enbd/images/private-banking/inspiring-whats-next/2023/Thought-Leadership/gcc_family_offices_must_adapt.jpg?la=en&h=467&w=700&hash=57B5B7DDF5EA47898807E532D3141778)  
##### GCC Family Offices Must Adapt, Manage Complex Needs To Succeed  
*This article from WealthBriefing is published in conjunction with Emirates NBD Private Banking and will be part of a series.*  
Single-family and multi-family offices (FO) in the Middle East must embrace a wider range of service offerings to meet members’ increasingly complex needs.  
Whether it is the rising prominence of women within these organisations or help with private market investments into areas such as tech, - ESG, the region’s FOs know they must adapt. Real estate investment – an important area for decades – remains pertinent but isn’t dominating attention as in the past. Younger family members appear to be captivated by digital and fintech sectors. They want a slice of the action and need guidance. That creates opportunities for wealth advisors, private banks and other organisations who can give help.

The Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) indicated what sort of services are in demand when in 2022 it announced the launch of its global family business and private wealth centre. It provides advisory and concierge services, education and training, outreach, and high-end networking, undertaking research, issuing publications, and providing dispute resolution assistance.  
From our conversations with industry figures, the Middle East is keen to learn best-practice ideas from more established family office markets, particularly in the US and in Europe. More of such cross-pollination of ideas is essential. In the US, for example, organisations such as the UHNW Institute have built ideas on the key skills and habits advisors must have to work with families. Groups such as the Family Wealth Alliance, a US pan-industry group, track remuneration of family office staff – there appears to be a dearth of such data in the Middle East. But this sort of information is vital for getting value and achieving results. Building these resources is also likely to be an important growth area as the family office sector evolves in the region.  
**Structures and models**

**Structures and models**  
One area to consider is the kind of structures that family offices should take. Globally, the most favoured structure is the limited liability partnership. This appears to fit with a need to remain flexible as younger generations succeed to business roles and management of wealth. According to a recent [global study](https://www.dentons.com/en/services-and-solutions/family-office-direct-investing-survey/family-offices-investment-strategies) of FOs worldwide by law firm Dentons, 53 per cent of them choose a limited liability entity that mix characteristics of a corporation with those of a partnership. Some 19 per cent each choose a personal holding company and a private trust company; in the US, 18 per cent choose a S Corporation; 17 per cent adopt an entity where two or more partners enter a business and are not liable for more than their investment; 14 per cent use a company as a "legal person" distinct from its members, with separate duties and liabilities, and 8 per cent go for "other" not defined structures.  
In certain cases, more “corporate” structures, based on accepting leadership roles, may make more sense, especially if there are tax issues.  
**Pressures and biases**

**Pressures and biases**  
As the world wrestles with inflation, evidence suggests the Middle East-based family offices fret particularly about price pressures. Dentons said 80 per cent of family offices in the region are more worried about inflation, while globally, 68 per cent of FOs are very concerned about inflation.) Regionally, FOs differ in how they use market falls as opportunities to buy back in. FOs in Asia Pacific (75 per cent), Latin America (58 per cent) and the Middle East (55 per cent) are most likely to be using market falls to buy equities, while those in North America (45 per cent) and Europe (42 per cent) are less likely to do so.  
The inflation worry means FOs will want to keep diversifying investment solutions to hedge inflation, such as in private markets (equity, credit, infrastructure, property, and commodities) and require top-class investment management solutions. Some family offices, even the larger MFOs, might not be able to do all this work alone.

For family offices that are outside the region, but looking to enter it, -should realise how they can gain deep insights around energy and real estate by talking to local business leaders. In the UAE, Saudi Arabia and other jurisdictions, business leaders understand these countries must adapt as the region contemplates a world less reliant on fossil fuels. The dramatic rise of Dubai, and the reform programme of the Saudi government [shows](https://www.wealthbriefing.com/html/article.php?id=197488#.ZIA6T3bMKM8) the Middle East is full of people eager to change and build new sectors. Family offices can seize these opportunities.  
**Inside or outside**  
Middle East family offices must be clear about what they can afford to do in-house and what they can outsource. As a rule, the bigger the family office, the less it needs to outsource (although it may still make sense to do so). In the US, the role of the outsourced chief investment office firm is well-established – this is not so in the Middle East. That’s a growth area to watch.

There are opportunities for outsourced CIOs to penetrate this market and offer solutions. The same applies to other outsourcing specialists such as in areas like bill payments, cybersecurity, physical security, digital tech support, cashflow management, healthcare expertise, concierge, property management, human resources, and philanthropy. We have spoken to firms building “family offices-as-a-service” models to offer standardised offerings in some of these areas so that family offices don’t have to build these from scratch. It looks as if the Middle East will be fruitful territory for elite service providers.

The Pink ATM is back. With Emirates NBD and Aster Clinics, Hospitals and Pharmacies | Emirates NBD > This year, we’re sharing their stories.

## This year, we’re sharing their stories.  
![Maya S.](https://cdn.emiratesnbd.com/assets/images/breast-cancer/icon-health_and_safety.png)  
#### Maya S.  
“I almost walked past the Pink ATM. But something made me stop, scan the QR code and book a screening.  
That decision changed my life.  
Doctors detected something early. I received treatment, and today I’m cancer-free.  
If you’ve been putting off your screening, please don’t wait.”  
![Omar H.](https://cdn.emiratesnbd.com/assets/images/breast-cancer/icon-stethoscope.png)  
#### Omar H.  
“I used to think breast cancer only affected women. Then I learnt that men could get it too.  
When I noticed something wasn’t right, I decided to get it checked. Thankfully, it wasn’t anything serious.  
But I learnt something important. If you notice something unusual, get checked.”  
![Nour K.](https://cdn.emiratesnbd.com/assets/images/breast-cancer/icon-self_improvement.png)  
#### Nour K.  
“I kept putting it off. The Pink ATM gave me the push to book an appointment. Thankfully, I was clear. I walked out of the clinic with something precious: peace of mind. If it’s been on your mind, go and get checked.”

text:
0% Installment Payment Plan Request | Emirates NBD > Quick Answers

## Quick Answers  
[Am I eligible for a 0% Installment Payment Plan?](#accordion-8838674b-1719-4ed4-8e61-3828d3f5fed3 "Am I eligible for a 0 Installment Payment Plan")  
You’re eligible if your purchase has been made with one of our **[participating merchants](/en/deals/0-epp)**.  
[Can I still earn reward points if I convert a transaction to a 0% interest Installment Payment Plan?](#accordion-f8cf5378-b422-49ef-a50a-21fe39a40552 "Can I still earn reward points if I convert a transaction to a 0 interest Installment Payment Plan")  
Rewards will be forfeited for transactions converted to a 0% IPP except for the following credit cards:  
* Skywards Credit Cards
* Skywards Business Credit Card
* Marriott Bonvoy Credit Cards
* dnata Credit Cards (transactions conducted at dnata outlets & dnata online)
* U by Emaar Credit Cards on Emaar spends
* LuLu Credit Cards on LuLu spends
* noon One Credit Cards on Noon platform spends
* Darna Credit Cards on Aldar spends
* Share Credit Cards on spends in Majid Al Futtaim (MAF) ecosystem
+ For spends outside MAF ecosystem, only the Share Platinum Variant will forfeit the points  
[Are there any processing fees for installment plans?](#accordion-5d0a6914-66bd-4eda-abe8-cc5b53504dbb "Are there any processing fees for installment plans")
title: 0% Installment Payment Plan Request | Emirates NBD

text:
0% Installment Payment Plan Request | Emirates NBD > Quick Answers

Regular Installment Payment Plan, Balance Conversion, and Loan on Card don’t have a processing fee, but a nominal interest rate applies based on your credit card history and usage. With the 0% interest Installment Payment Plan there could be a one-time processing fee of 51.45 (inclusive of VAT) per transaction. For more details, read more about our [**fees and charges**](/-/media/enbd/files/others/fees-and-charges/cards/emiratesnbd_credit_card_fees_charges.pdf).  
[Can I cancel my installment plan?](#accordion-db3da5c8-1edc-4fe2-b949-6e54efff5931 "Can I cancel my installment plan")  
Yes, you can cancel your installment plan through Mobile Banking and Online Banking.
Before cancelling your plan, you will have to settle the remaining principal outstanding plus a foreclosure fee of 1% of the principal outstanding and 5% VAT.  
[I want to follow up on a previous request.](#accordion-197ad0cf-7b2c-483a-9399-37688d324d5c "I want to follow up on a previous request.")  
You can track your previous request by calling us on [**+971 600 54 0000**](tel:+971600540000) and when prompted, say ‘follow up on my request’.

# Terms & Conditions  
## Emirates NBD Debit Cards PIN Activation Campaign – Primary Cards  
**Promotion Period:**  1st – 31st May 2023  
**Applicable for:**  Selected Emirates NBD Visa Personal Banking Debit Cardholders  
**Qualifying Customer:**  
* This promotion is open only to preselected Emirates NBD Visa Debit Cardholders (“Cardholders/ Cardholder”)
* The eligible Cardholders will receive specific communication from the Bank through SMS, online and mobile banking, with respect to the specific promotion period. Enrollment rights are reserved and solely determined by the bank.  
**Qualifying Criteria and Reward Details:**  
* To qualify cardholders will have to activate their Debit card and make Point of Sale/Online spends on their card during the campaign period. No minimum spend cap to qualify.
* Cardholders should also register/opt in for this promotion. Customer can opt in through Mobile or Online Banking or by sending SMS “ACTPM” to 4456 from the mobile number registered with Emirates NBD.
* Rewards will be 10% Back on spends in form of cashback with a cap of 100 will be credited per customer with a qualifying card. No replicate winners.
* Only the first 500 customers to qualify will receive the rewards.
* Transactions on the card in the form of reversals, refunds or disputed purchases during the campaign period will be excluded from the Qualifying Spends/ transactions.
