Islamic Deposit Products | Islamic Banking  | Emirates NBD > Mudaraba Savings Account

### Mudaraba Savings Account  
**How it Works:**  
Mudaraba is a special kind of partnership where you (‘Rab Al Mal’) provide money to the bank (‘Mudarib’) for investing in Shari’ah compliant assets that generate a specific income.  
This income is shared between the investor, who is the account holder, and the bank, i.e. the Mudarib or trust manager. It operates under the ‘unrestricted’ Mudaraba principle and is designed to generate regular earnings in a Shari’ah compliant manner. The actual profit is distributed as per the agreed ratio at the end of each quarter. At Emirates NBD, we are authorised to invest the money according to the Shari’ah principles of Mudaraba.  
![msaf](/-/media/enbd/images/islamic-banking/islamicbanking_savings_account-flip.jpg?la=en&h=1400&w=2800&hash=DE3016CB2AEA21DDF559D4F7B52E2672)  
### Mudaraba Savings Account  
The account operates under the ‘unrestricted’ Mudaraba principle and offers very competitive profit rates without limiting your banking transactions.  
**Features:**  
* No Minimum balance
* Available in AED and USD
* Minimum tenor of 30 days to avail profit
* Available to individuals only
* Quarterly profit distribution to the account
* No cheque book issued

### Wakala Deposits  
**How it Works:**  
Wakala is an agency contract, where the customer (Principal) appoints the bank as his agent to carry out investment activities as per an agreed plan and generate an expected profit rate  
In Wakala contracts, the actual profit is distributed according to the profit ratio agreed upfront. The bank or ‘wakil’ is able to specify expected returns from the funds provided by the customer.  
![wdf](/-/media/enbd/images/islamic-banking/wakalasavingsaccount_banner_ar.jpg?la=en&h=700&w=1440&hash=A64D349CD8640AF8C484BC7DF1DAAE57)  
### Wakala Deposits  
Invest and gain profit from Shari’ah approved activities with profit rates based on the investments and the flexibility of choosingthe tenor.  
**Features:**  
* Available in AED and USD
* Minimum deposit of 10,000 or equivalent in USD
* Shari'ah compliant
* Available to individualsand non-individuals

# Defer your loan payments  
You can apply for a loan deferment for your personal or auto loan
title: Defer your Loan Payment  | Auto Loan and Personal Loan Deferment | Emirates NBD

text:
Defer your Loan Payment  | Auto Loan and Personal Loan Deferment | Emirates NBD > Before you start

## Before you start  
Important information to note before you start:  
* **Personal and auto loan:**If you choose to defer your auto or personal loan instalment, the final instalment amount may be higher than the other instalments in your repayment schedule.
* The loan tenure may be extended in line with the deferment, as outlined in your loan agreement.
* **Home loan:** For home loan, deferment of the first installment is not applicable. Interest will continue to apply on the deferred installment, and the loan tenure may be extended by one month.
* This service under the Deferral Relief Programme is **free of charge**.
* Once your request is submitted, it will be processed within 7 working days. Upon completion of your request, you will receive an SMS confirmation on your registered mobile number
* Please have your account or loan number ready for verification.  
To request a **personal** or **auto loan** deferment, click **[here](/en/self-service/deferral-relief-program/apply)**.  
To request a **home loan** deferment, click **[here](/en/self-service/deferral-relief-program-home-loan/apply)**.  
Refer to the Deferral Relief Programme FAQs **[here](/-/media/enbd/files/pdf/deferral-relief-programme-faq.pdf)**.

# The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth  
23 December 2022  
[Share](javascript:void(0); "Share")  
![theregionaliposurgeisanopportunitytomultiplywealth](/-/media/enbd/images/private-banking/inspiring-whats-next/PB_IPO_banner.jpg?la=en&h=467&w=700&hash=16F375310A56DA5DBC000E952CB660F0)  
##### The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth  
*Private bankers and wealth advisers are offering access, analysis, and guidance to MENA’s wealthiest segments on the new issuances in the region*  
Equity markets in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region have been on a roll in 2022, with 24 initial public offerings (IPOs) raising USD 13.5 billion in the first half of the year, an increase of 2,952% compared to the same period in 2021. Total equity issuance as we end the year is estimated to be close to USD 20 billion.  
Globally, **[IPOs raised](https://www.ey.com/en_qa/news/2022/08/24-mena-ipos-raise-us-13-5-billion-in-h1-2022)** USD 95.4 billion during H1 2022, a drop of 58% compared to H1 2021. While global markets witnessed declining valuations and higher volatility caused by geopolitical tensions and macroeconomic factors, MENA markets continue to be an emerging opportunity, with several more IPOs planned for 2023.
title: The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth
section: The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth

text:
The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth > The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth

MENA IPOs in 2022 have largely been heavily oversubscribed, defying the global trend and confirming that investors still have an appetite for growth. For instance, Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) raised over USD 6 billion and was oversubscribed 37 times. Borouge raised USD 2 billion with an oversubscription of almost 42 times. The TECOM Group raised USD 454 million and saw an oversubscription of more than 21 times. Salik, the toll operator, was oversubscribed 47 times. Divestments by the Dubai Government are adding to private listings in the UAE. Saudi Arabia has seen a broadening of sector representation including the healthcare and retail space following Saudi Aramco’s mega 2019 offering.  
![](/-/media/enbd/images/private-banking/inspiring-whats-next/PB_IPO_1.jpg)  
This pattern has been an opportunity as well as a challenge for the private banking industry, especially in the UAE, where the number of high net worth investors continues to grow. As many as **[4,000 millionaires](https://www.henleyglobal.com/publications/henley-global-citizens-report/2022-q2)** are expected to move to the UAE in 2022.
title: The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth
section: The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth

text:
The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth > The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth

Equity markets make up a large composition of investor portfolios,ranging from 20% for conservative to 60% for adventurous profiles when it comes to wealth management. IPOs offer some of the biggest potential opportunities when they combine quality business attributes with compelling valuations. While some IPO underwriters may focus on institutional investors, many flagship deals are also offered to retail investors. High net worth individuals share characteristics with both.  
Governments in the GCC have led the charge in expanding their equity capital markets by **[increasing liquidity](https://www.globalcapital.com/article/2ax5eikn4tvah7ncc27sw/equity/equity-people-and-markets/beware-deterioration-in-asset-quality-as-gulf-ipo-boom-continues)** and the flow of foreign capital, as they diversify their economies away from a dependence on hydrocarbons. It is in every country’s interest to ensure that capital markets are as deep and sophisticated as possible. This has ensured a steady supply of high-quality IPOs in recent months, including those from state-owned companies.  
![](/-/media/enbd/images/private-banking/inspiring-whats-next/PB_IPO_2.jpg)
title: The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth
section: The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth

text:
The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth > The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth

![](/-/media/enbd/images/private-banking/inspiring-whats-next/PB_IPO_2.jpg)  
Wealthy investors – both individual and institutional – view this as an opportunity to diversify their investments by getting in on the inception of flotations by companies with strong business models. Post listing, 75% of recent IPOs regionally are trading above the IPO price. One of the risks associated with such a strong flow of valuable IPOs is the possibility of companies with less robust business models also taking advantage of the deepening pool of capital. The well-defined government strategy to expand and diversify the equity capital market by bringing superstar state-owned entities to IPO generally creates the momentum that paves the way for privately-owned businesses to follow suit.  
It is then up to private bankers and wealth advisors to ensure that HNWI investments are putting their money into the most valuable options. This acts as a safeguard against any deterioration in asset quality. Private bankers perform this function using a three-pronged strategy: giving individual and institutional clients the right intelligence through research; giving them access to the opportunity by ensuring they are early investors; and advising them on the right price and time to sell.  
![](/-/media/enbd/images/private-banking/inspiring-whats-next/PB_IPO_3.jpg)
title: The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth
section: The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth

text:
The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth > The regional IPO surge is an opportunity to multiply wealth

![](/-/media/enbd/images/private-banking/inspiring-whats-next/PB_IPO_3.jpg)  
With the region’s equity markets showing no signs of cooling off in the short term, the opportunity for a surge in wealth creation has, so to speak, come home for the region’s HNWI. Those who had earlier sought to multiply wealth by investing in global high-growth equity markets can now do so in their own countries. This has the additional benefit of local HNWI investors supporting the expansion of their own markets and economies.

## How to make a claim  
* For assistance in submitting a claim under this policy, please contact ADNIC.
* **ADNIC Contact Centre:**
+ 1. Claim and policy information should be raised with at [**800 8040**](tel:+971600540000) or [**service-emiratesnbd@adnic.ae**](mailto:service-emiratesnbd@adnic.ae)
+ 2. Death and Disability claims must be reported within 365 days of the event with a complete claim form to [**lifeclaims@adnic.ae**](mailto:lifeclaims@adnic.ae)
* Upon receipt of claim notification, ADNIC would register the claim, allocate and advise a claim number and required documents to the customer  
**Please remember all requested documents are essential for processing the claim via ADNIC.**

# Transfer money internationally with Western Union, through Emirates NBD's Online and Mobile Banking platforms  
* [Key highlights](#tab_bsa7c93cfd-3e97-472a-abbc-3cf1937c4ce6 "Key highlights")  
Instant money transfer to over **500,000** agent locations worldwide:  
* Available through Online and Mobile Banking
* Transfer money to more than 200 countries and territories worldwide
* Only individual customers can transfer money using this service
* The transaction limit is**25,000** (or equivalent) per transaction  
As per Western Union guidelines, from 6thAugust, 2020 recipients in Lebanon need to pay an additional 2% cash handling fee (on the sent principal amount), which will be collected by agents in Lebanon. For transactions done in USD, the money will be deducted from the principal amount at payout.

Connect with thousands of financial institutions.

## SWIFT for corporates  
With SWIFT, corporates can connect with thousands of financial institutions to interact and settle transactions in an easy, secure manner.  
![1](/-/media/enbd/images/cib/checklistpad_icon.png?la=en&h=200&w=200&hash=9E0CBF3E52D3361EE53B7EDF33320483)

Fast & secure exchange of instructions.  
![3](/-/media/enbd/images/cib/laptopgraph_icon.png?la=en&h=200&w=200&hash=64FC9F45178488EF15DEDC3E5CAE010B)  
Single-channel platform.  
![4](/-/media/enbd/images/cib/shakehands_icon.png?la=en&h=200&w=200&hash=E076660C3E068AFFFF66EDC3381237CB)  
Adaptable to multiple business solutions and flows.  
[Know more](/-/media/enbd/files/cib/2022/swift_for_corporates_cib.pdf "SWIFT for corporates")  
![Promo  Standardised Corporate Environment](/-/media/enbd/images/cib/swift-for-corporates/score_banner.jpg?la=en&h=1400&w=2800&hash=545B05D4D596C8AE00256D780CE486A3)  
#### Standardised Corporate Environment (SCORE)  
The Standardised Corporate Environment (SCORE) is based on a closed user group, administered by SWIFT, where corporates can interact with financial institutions.  
Emirates NBD SWIFT offers two types of services – SWIFT FIN and SWIFT FileACT.

text:
Defer Your Personal and Auto Loan Payments with online banking | Emirates NBD > FAQs

## FAQs  
[Can I defer my first loan installment?](#faqs-can-i-defer-my-first-loan-installment "Can I defer my first loan installment")  
No, your loan's first installment can’t be deferred.  
[How many times can I defer my personal and auto loan?](#faqs-how-many-times-can-i-defer-my-personal-and-auto-loan "How many times can I defer my personal and auto loan")  
Only two deferrals are allowed for personal loan per loan cycle year and they can’t be consecutive. Only one deferral is allowed for an auto loan per loan cycle year.  
[How can I make a loan deferment if my mode of payment is PDC or UAEDDS?](#faqs-how-can-i-make-a-loan-deferment-if-my-mode-of-payment-is-pdc-or-uaedds "How can I make a loan deferment if my mode of payment is PDC or UAEDDS")  
There are no deferments on PDC and DSS loans.  
[I would like to defer my home loan. What should I do?](#faqs-i-would-like-to-defer-my-home-loan-what-should-i-do "I would like to defer my home loan. What should I do")  
Deferments are not permitted for home loans. However, if you have suffered job loss, salary reduction, etc. you can write to [mortgages@emiratesnbd.com](mailto:mortgages@emiratesnbd.com) with supporting documents we will look into the case and within approximately 5-7 working days from the date all documents are given.

Balance Conversion Plan (BCP) Request | Emirates NBD > Quick Answers

## Quick Answers  
[Am I eligible for Balance Conversion Plan?](#accordion-d7b3972b-9555-4fe9-979d-60fbfdbee08b "Am I eligible for Balance Conversion Plan")  
You need to be the primary cardholder to apply for a Balance Conversion and you can apply for a minimum amount of 1,000.  
[Are there any processing fees for installment plans?](#accordion-d955d780-5a40-45c9-b738-95bd2ade15ca "Are there any processing fees for installment plans")  
Regular Installment Payment Plan, Balance Conversion, and Loan on Card don’t have a processing fee, but a nominal interest rate applies based on your credit card history and usage.
With the 0% interest Installment Payment Plan there could be a one-time processing fee of 51.45 (inclusive of VAT) per transaction. For more details, read more about our [**fees and charges**](/-/media/enbd/files/others/fees-and-charges/cards/emiratesnbd_credit_card_fees_charges.pdf).  
[Can I cancel my installment plan?](#accordion-f8893ac1-b140-49ce-a676-a0d7ba805a87 "Can I cancel my installment plan")  
Yes, you can cancel your installment plan through Mobile Banking and Online Banking.
Before cancelling your plan, you will have to settle the remaining principal outstanding plus a foreclosure fee of 1% of the principal outstanding and 5% VAT.

[How to open a UAE Bank Account in minutes?](#accordion-39b09f8d-5573-4f80-949c-73d150850f74 "How to open a UAE Bank Account in minutes")  
Opening a UAE bank account in the UAE is straightforward with Emirates NBD. You just need a few documents to open your account online:  
* **For UAE Residents:**
+ Emirates ID
+ Valid passport
+ Proof of address (e.g., utility bill or tenancy contract)
+ Salary transfer letter or recent payslips (for salary accounts)
* **For Non-Residents:**
+ Valid passport with visa page
+ Proof of address
+ Reference letter from your home country's bank
+ Recent bank statements  
[What’s the difference between Current and Savings Accounts?](#accordion-0689eac4-31d6-4184-972f-d5426aa82724 "Whats the difference between Current and Savings Accounts")  
Current and savings accounts serve different financial purposes:  
* **Current Accounts** are ideal for your day-to-day banking transactions, such as local and international money transfers, bill payments, including facilities like cheque books and overdrafts.

## Redeeming Business Rewards Points  
Emirates Business Rewards programme offers enhanced flexibility with no restrictions. The Points can be used on any fare type, on any flight or any class giving a wider range of options.  
Your Business Rewards Points earned on your Emirates NBD Business Rewards Credit Card can be checked online. Just visit [**emirates.com/businessrewards**](https://www.emirates.com/english/business-rewards/)and log in to your Emirates Business Rewards account.  
Remember, you will need your existing Skywards account number and password to log in, even into your Business Rewards account. This is because your Business Rewards account is linked to the original Skywards account.

## Rewards Capping  
The number of points you can earn is based on your credit card type.  
- **Credit Card**: **Priority Banking Visa Infinite**; **Cap per statement**: 5,000 Plus Points
- **Credit Card**: **Visa Infinite**  **Go4it Platinum**; **Cap per statement**: 3,000 Plus Points
- **Credit Card**: **Visa Platinum**  **Mastercard Platinum**  **Visa Flexi**  **Go4it Gold**  **Diners Club**  **Duo\*\***; **Cap per statement**: 2,000 Plus Points
- **Credit Card**: **Titanium**; **Cap per statement**: 1,000 Plus Points
- **Credit Card**: **Webshopper**; **Cap per statement**: 500 Plus Points  
\*Category wise earning will be applicable on both domestic and international spends, as defined by VISA/MasterCard/Diners Club International.  
\*\*Effective 5April 2025, you can earn a maximum of 500 Plus Points per statement.

text:
Earn Plus Points | Support | Emirates NBD > FAQs

## FAQs  
[Do all transactions on my credit card earn Plus Points?](#faqs-do-all-transactions-on-my-credit-card-earn-plus-points "Do all transactions on my credit card earn Plus Points")  
Only retail spends earn Plus Points. Loans on your card, cash advances, bank fees and charges, balance transfers and 0% installment payment plans don’t earn points. [Click here](/en/help-and-support/redeeming-plus-points)to learn more about eligible transactions.  
[How long are Plus Points valid for?](#faqs-how-long-are-plus-points-valid-for "How long are Plus Points valid for")  
Plus Points don’t expire as long as you have an active Emirates NBD card. Once you redeem them for Frequent Flyer Miles, the terms and conditions of your frequent flyer programme apply.  
[What happens to the rewards earned on my supplementary credit card?](#faqs-what-happens-to-the-rewards-earned-on-my-supplementary-credit-card "What happens to the rewards earned on my supplementary credit card")  
Rewards earned for transactions on your supplementary credit cards are transferred to your primary credit card.  
[Will I lose the rewards I have earned if my card is replaced?](#faqs-will-i-lose-the-rewards-i-have-earned-if-my-card-is-replaced "Will I lose the rewards I have earned if my card is replaced")  
No, you won't lose your rewards, they'll just be transferred to your new Emirates NBD card.

## Manage your credit card limits  
Your credit card limit is assigned by the bank after taking several factors into consideration including the type of credit card, eligibility, financial history and debt burden ratio.
title: Manage your business credit card limits

text:
Manage your business credit card limits > Understanding your limits

## Understanding your limits  
Your **credit card limit** is the maximum amount you can spend using your credit card. The amount you spend and need to repay, at least in part before your payment due date, is referred to as your **outstanding balance** or **utilised limit** and the remainder is your **available credit limit**.  
If you hold one or more supplementary credit cards, these cards will utilise a percentage of your total limit. For example, if your credit card has a total limit of 100,000 and you assign your supplementary credit card 10% of your limit, the supplementary card holder can use only 10,000.

## Increase your primary credit card limit  
To apply for a credit limit increase on your credit card you must meet the following criteria:  
* Your card should be active
* Your documents need to be updated
* You should be holding the card for at least 6 months  
Use one of the options below to apply for a limit increase on your card:  
**Phone Banking:**  
Call [+971 600 54 0009](tel:971600540009) and when prompted, say ‘increase credit card limit’  
Keep these documents ready to complete your request.  
**Online Banking**  
* Log into [Online Banking](https://login1.emiratesnbd.com/obweb/common/banknet.jsf)
* Click on **Online Advice** and go to your **Private Wall**
* Select the topic, enter your comment and **Post**  
One of our representatives will get in touch with you within 24 hours.  
Keep these documents ready to complete your request.  
**Mobile Banking**  
* Log in to Mobile Banking
* Click on the **hamburger icon** on the top left of the app

* Select **Inquiries** and then the type of inquiry
* Enter your request and click **Send**  
One of our representatives will get in touch with you within 24 hours.  
Keep these documents ready to complete your request.

## Increase or decrease your supplementary credit card limit  
Only a primary credit card holder can increase or decrease their supplementary credit limit. You can do this by changing the percentage of the primary credit card’s total limit that has been assigned to the supplementary credit card. Please note that the change in percentage will have to be in multiples of 5.  
To request a change in your Supplementary Credit Card limit, choose one of the options below:  
**Phone Banking:**

## FAQs  
[Will I receive a new credit card once my limit is increased?](#faqs-will-i-receive-a-new-credit-card-once-my-limit-is-increased "Will I receive a new credit card once my limit is increased")  
No, your credit limit will be increased on your existing credit card.  
[How can I track my supplementary card holder’s credit limit utilisation?](#faqs-how-can-i-track-my-supplementary-card-holders-credit-limit-utilisation "How can I track my supplementary card holders credit limit utilisation")  
You can do this by viewing your supplementary credit card’s limit details or transaction history through Online and Mobile Banking. Your supplementary card holder’s transactions will be listed in your monthly credit card statements as well.  
[What’s the maximum amount that I can increase my credit card limit by?](#faqs-whats-the-maximum-amount-that-i-can-increase-my-credit-card-limit-by "Whats the maximum amount that I can increase my credit card limit by")  
Everyone’s credit limit differs as this is based on a number of factors. The bank will always process your request for the maximum eligible amount.  
[What happens if I use my entire credit card limit](#faqs-what-happens-if-i-use-my-entire-credit-card-limit "What happens if I use my entire credit card limit")

text:
Manage your business credit card limits > FAQs

Emirates NBD Credit Cards have a buffer limit which allows you to complete a purchase that is higher than your current available credit limit. Based on the type of credit card you hold, your buffer limit can range between 3% and 15% of your total credit limit.  
Spending more than your assigned credit limit will incur over-limit charges.  
Always keep track of your credit card transactions and available limit. It’s easy via Online and Mobile Banking.  
**Online Banking:** Go to **My Finances > Cards**  
**Mobile Banking:** Click![](/-/media/enbd/images/help-and-support/icons/hamburger-200x200.png) and then Credit Cards.  
[How much of my credit limit can be used for cash advances?](#faqs-how-much-of-my-credit-limit-can-be-used-for-cash-advances "How much of my credit limit can be used for cash advances")  
You can use up to 75% of your total credit limit for cash advances on business credit cards and 50% of your total credit limit for cash advances on any other credit card.  
[Is it possible to transfer some of my credit limit from one of my credit cards to another?](#faqs-is-it-possible-to-transfer-some-of-my-credit-limit-from-one-of-my-credit-cards-to-another "Is it possible to transfer some of my credit limit from one of my credit cards to another")  
You can only transfer a portion of your credit limit from a non-Web Shopper credit card to your Web Shopper card. You can’t transfer credit limit between non-Web Shopper credit cards.

# Financial benefits on your Emirates NBD cards  
Learn more about your Emirates NBD card’s financial benefits and learn how to avail them  
Manage your finances better by using the interest-free days and flexible payment options on your Emirates NBD credit card.  
**Interest-free days**  
Spend now and pay after 55 days with zero interest if you pay the entire outstanding balance by the due date.  
**Flexible payment option**  
Enjoy the flexibility of paying a minimum of 5% of your outstanding balance and carry forward the balance to next statement. You can choose to pay from 5%, 10%, 25%, 50% or 100% of the outstanding balance every month on or before your due date. Learn more [here](/en/help-and-support/manage-your-monthly-credit-card-payments).  
**Instant cash withdrawal worldwide**  
Enjoy instant access to cash up to 50% of your credit card limit at over 810,000 ATMs worldwide that display the Visa or MasterCard symbols. Your card will be charged a nominal cash advance fee.  
**Installment payment plan**  
You need not struggle to pay your credit card dues with our convenient Installment Payment Plan. Learn more [here](/en/help-and-support/installment-payment-plan).

# Smart cities bring better life  
01 June 2021  
[Share](javascript:void(0); "Share")  
![Smart cities bring better life](https://cdn.emiratesnbd.com/en/assets/images/smart_cities_010721_img1_thumb.jpg)  
##### Smart cities bring better life  
A select group of metro areas are developing not randomly but intelligently, by combining master planning with high-tech. The aim: longer, happier, wealthier lives for their residents.  
Smart phones, smart watches, smart cars – of course they are not actually alive, but compared to their less-intelligent alternatives, they are able to think. So it is, too, with cities. Smart ones figure out how to deliver a personalised, best quality of life to their residents.  
**Intelligent life – how does that work?**
title: Smart cities bring better life

text:
Smart cities bring better life > Smart cities bring better life

**Intelligent life – how does that work?**  
Smart starts at home. A thoughtful thermostat gives just the right temperature and humidity, sensible sensors control lighting and access. Not in just one house, rather the entire neighbourhood, and this coordinates with local utilities to minimise cost and balance load (that’s why clothes- and dishwashers kick in at night, automatically). Smart continues in the commute: computers organise journeys to minimise jams, smog and travel time. Your car parks itself – no scrapes, no hassle, no searching for a space. At work and at play, the city foresees your needs. As you walk in their shops, retailers know you and what you want (based on sensors and past purchases). There is super-fast Internet and lightning-speed video – everywhere. Green and quiet spots for sport and down-time are part of the landscape: parks, squares, cafes, gyms, pools, beaches, places of worship, libraries – all in easy reach. Noise, air and water pollution have been engineered to a minimum. Aaaaah, can you feel your blood pressure falling? Ok, if not, a body-monitor keeps you in remote touch with your physician, just in case. Better health with fewer trips to the doctor!  
![The Edge](//cdn.emiratesnbd.com/en/assets/images/smart_cities_010721_img2_thumb.jpg)  
**Not an accident**
title: Smart cities bring better life

text:
Smart cities bring better life > Smart cities bring better life

![The Edge](//cdn.emiratesnbd.com/en/assets/images/smart_cities_010721_img2_thumb.jpg)  
**Not an accident**  
Smart starts with urban planning: attractive cities are made, not born. This is the consensus of academics and analysts, such as those at the Smart City Observatory, part of the renowned Institute for Management Development. According to its annual ‘Smart City Index’ study, smart cities are designed both to boost the benefits and dampen the downsides of urban living. They offer built-in relaxation spaces, high air and water quality, integrated transport and a holistic approach to city life. Simultaneously, they apply ‘thinking’ technology to the maximum; they delegate repetitive, endless, dirty tasks to computers and robots. This frees people to be creative, productive – even joyful. The key to it all, says the Smart City Observatory, is keeping a balance between technology and humanity. Not a city with no soul, where machines rule; neither a city of squalor, where human excess dominates.  
**And the highest IQ metropolis is?**
title: Smart cities bring better life

text:
Smart cities bring better life > Smart cities bring better life

**And the highest IQ metropolis is?**  
Smart-city surveys (there are several) reward a clutch of perennial winners: Amsterdam, Auckland, Copenhagen, Geneva, Helsinki, Oslo, Singapore, Taipei City and Zurich. Seeing is believing, as residents and visitors testify these are some of the world’s best places to live. Both from a personal or an investment viewpoint, the numbers tell a story: between the Smart City Index’s 2020 top city, Singapore, and its laggard, Lagos at number 109: average lives are 50% longer, incomes and wealth are 8-9 times larger, and, according to the World Happiness Report, people are four times as satisfied with their lives. So, in which would you choose to live or invest?  
![The Edge](//cdn.emiratesnbd.com/en/assets/images/smart_cities_010721_img3_thumb.jpg)  
**No gulf to the Gulf**
title: Smart cities bring better life

text:
Smart cities bring better life > Smart cities bring better life

![The Edge](//cdn.emiratesnbd.com/en/assets/images/smart_cities_010721_img3_thumb.jpg)  
**No gulf to the Gulf**  
Hot in the race and relatively high in the ranks of ‘smart-ville’ are three GCC locations. Dubai, with its 2040 vision of being the best city to live in, is devoted to making life seamless, efficient, safe and personalised; Abu Dhabi is accentuating the same, and is ranked at a similar IQ. Both will benefit from the Dubai-Abu Dhabi hyperloop – it could be called smart transport in action. The $6-billion train-cum-jet will shuttle the 150 kilometres between those metros in 10 minutes. Then there is the NEOM project. Nestled by the Red Sea in northwest Saudi Arabia, this city-in-planning aims to accommodate industry, finance, services and some 1 million inhabitants by 2030. The $500-billion metropolis aims to be smarter than any other. So clever that no cars and no roads will be needed: everything anyone needs will be within a 5-minute walk! More than smart – it just might be genius.

# The immense potential inherent in the Great Wealth Transfer  
01 June 2022  
[Share](javascript:void(0); "Share")  
![The immense potential inherent in the Great Wealth Transfer](https://cdn.emiratesnbd.com/en/assets/images/immense_potential_great_wealth_transfer_img.jpg)  
##### The immense potential inherent in the Great Wealth Transfer  
By Saod Mohammed Obaidalla, Executive Vice President and Head of Private Banking - June 2022  
![](//cdn.emiratesnbd.com/en/assets/images/immense_potential_great_wealth_transfer_imgg.jpg)  
Regional trends indicate that Millennials and Gen Z are taking their place in the boardrooms of family businesses, even as the law evolves to support the continued contribution of this sector. It is crucial that wealth advisory be customized for the new generation, says **Saod Obaidalla, Executive Vice President and Head of Private Banking, Emirates NBD**  
The world is currently experiencing the Great Wealth Transfer, during which the world’s wealthiest individuals, each with a net worth of more than USD 5 million, will transfer an estimated [**USD 18.3 trillion**](https://go.wealthx.com/download-preservation-and-succession-family-wealth-transfer-2021) to their children by the year 2030. This figure represents one-fourth of the global wealth of USD 62 trillion held by high-net-worth individuals (HNWIs). - we add the infographic talking of this line here, instead of the text.  
![](//cdn.emiratesnbd.com/en/assets/images/PB_Insights_imgg1.jpg)
title: The immense potential inherent in the Great Wealth Transfer
section: The immense potential inherent in the Great Wealth Transfer

text:
The immense potential inherent in the Great Wealth Transfer > The immense potential inherent in the Great Wealth Transfer

![](//cdn.emiratesnbd.com/en/assets/images/PB_Insights_imgg1.jpg)  
The UAE’s leadership, from the time of the founding fathers, has always believed in the potential of youth to change the world for the better, entrusting the young with a place in the [**driver’s**](http://wam.ae/en/details/1395302627017) seat when it comes to development. The [**Emirati model**](https://wam.ae/en/details/1395302797926) of youth empowerment treats the young as the most cherished assets for ensuring creativity and innovation, while enshrining the positive values of society.  
**A different approach**  
The generational wealth transfer has implications for wealth managers so that the great potential of this transition can be realized. Wealth advisors must adapt to the many ways in which the [**Millennial**](https://www.weforum.org/agenda/2021/11/millennials-world-regional-breakdown/) or Gen Z investor differs from older counterparts, particularly in view of [**findings**](https://www.ey.com/en_gl/family-enterprise/how-the-worlds-largest-family-businesses-are-proving-their-resilience) that suggest that one in five businesses have a next generation member (aged 40 or younger) on the board or on the management team.

Millennials, for instance, are starting out with the greatest amount of [**formal education**](https://www.brookings.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/Generations-Working-Paper-2.pdf) of any generation in history. Coming of age in a digital, borderless world, their concerns are more global than those of previous generations. In a multi-cultural nation such as the UAE, it is not surprising that this generation has embraced [**diversity**](https://www.pewresearch.org/social-trends/2018/11/15/early-benchmarks-show-post-millennials-on-track-to-be-most-diverse-best-educated-generation-yet/) in investments, markets, and in management styles. These inheritors have the potential to globalize a business; in fact, [**58%**](https://www.pwc.com/m1/en/publications/middle-east-family-business-survey.html) of Middle East family businesses consider expansion into new markets a top priority.  
![](//cdn.emiratesnbd.com/en/assets/images/PB_Insights_imgg2.jpg)

![](//cdn.emiratesnbd.com/en/assets/images/PB_Insights_imgg2.jpg)  
As Millennials and Gen Z begin to accumulate wealth, their investment needs are likely to transform the institutional wealth management function. [**Impact**](https://www2.deloitte.com/uk/en/blog/deloitte-private/2020/investing-in-impact-a-strategy-for-next-generation-family-offices.html) investing, which combines financial returns with social and environmental benefits, is seeing an upsurge in interest, with [**59%**](https://www.pwc.com/m1/en/publications/middle-east-family-business-survey.html) of the region’s family businesses ready to take the lead in sustainable business practices. Investments in emerging technologies and digital transformation and assets are also gaining traction.  
![](//cdn.emiratesnbd.com/en/assets/images/PB_Insights_imgg3.jpg)  
**Regulatory support**  
With preservation and innovation as the two pillars ensuring the future of family businesses, UAE laws have kept pace to support and enhance the role of family offices in the diversification and growth of the national economy.

The immense potential inherent in the Great Wealth Transfer > The immense potential inherent in the Great Wealth Transfer

The Onshore [**Trust**](https://www.tamimi.com/law-update-articles/uae-at-the-forefront-of-legislative-development/) Law introduced in 2020 puts in place frameworks for the organization of family offices in the UAE and abroad to ensure stable and sustainable asset protection and succession planning. Also in 2020, Dubai introduced an opt-in law to regulate [**family**](https://www.mediaoffice.ae/en/news/2020/August/19-08/Mohammed-bin-Rashid-issues-Law) business ownership. The law not only [**underscores**](https://www2.deloitte.com/content/dam/Deloitte/xe/Documents/tax/me_walid-chniara-comments-law-No.9-of-2020-LexisNexis-09092020.pdf) the importance of family, enshrining a collaborative approach, but also provides for the new generation’s entrepreneurial vision.  
Dispute resolution too has been in the spotlight, with Decree No. 34 of 2021 concerning the Dubai International Arbitration Centre (DIAC) making significant changes to arbitral institutions in Dubai. Issued in 2022, Abu Dhabi’s new family business ownership [**governance law**](https://www.mediaoffice.abudhabi/en/government-affairs/khalifa-bin-zayed-issues-new-family-business-ownership-governance-law/) addresses the issue of continuity in the contribution of the thriving sector to the economy even as it facilitates a smooth transition to the succeeding generation.

Globally, family businesses and family offices remain the the largest contributors to GDP, and the largest employers in the private sector. They hold the key to economic growth and well-being. Being attuned to the needs of those who will be entrusted to manage these businesses in future will usher in better business practices, while delivering results that ensure the continued relevance of advisory services across generations.

text:
Steady Saver Deposit | Emirates NBD > Requirements and documents for opening an account

## Requirements and documents for opening an account  
[UAE Nationals](#accordion-ac70c5e5-ae81-475b-b9ac-d79cb5481205 "UAE Nationals")  
* **Identification**
+ Original Emirates ID and copy
+ Copy of passport
* **In case of a salary transfer account, we’ll need one of the following documents:**
+ Copy of Labour card
+ Copy of Employee ID
+ Latest salary letter
+ Copy of employment visa page from passport  
[Expats](#accordion-94f21629-400f-4a70-9e22-e696a22fc2d1 "Expats")  
* **Identification**
+ Original Emirates ID and copy
+ Copy of passport
* **In case of a salary transfer account, we’ll need one of the following documents:**
+ Salary transfer letter (not more than 30 days from date of issue for non-government companies. For government companies, validity as mentioned in the letter.)
+ Copy of appointment letter or contract
+ Copy of payslip (less than months old)
+ Statement with previous month’s salary
+ **For bulk accounts:** consolidated letter from HR (with salary of each employee mentioned)  
[Non-residents](#accordion-006cbba0-ea8d-4b84-a92c-74aebc98f3a7 "Nonresidents")  
* **Passport and copy with visa page and one of the following documents**
+ Utility bill (not more than 3 months old)
+ Bank statements (not more than 3 months old, and you can print these off online banking too)
title: Steady Saver Deposit | Emirates NBD

text:
Unlock your Online and Mobile Banking  | Support | Emirates NBD > Activate your blocked banking profile

## Activate your blocked banking profile  
If your Online or Mobile Banking profile is blocked, here are some possible reasons and what you can do about them:  
* **You entered a wrong password multiple times**  
[Reset your password](/en/help-and-support/reset-your-digital-banking-password)instantly.
* **You answered your secret question wrongly multiple times**  
[Reset your secret questions](/sitecore/service/notfound.aspx?item=web%3a%7bE6D2CDC4-EE4A-4342-8DC1-8AC49428E04A%7d%40en)instantly.
* **Your Online/Mobile Banking profile has been compromised, and the bank has blocked access for your safety**  
Call us from [your registered mobile number](/en/help-and-support/update-your-registered-mobile-number)and verify yourself with your PIN. When prompted, say 'issue with online/mobile banking' and we'll guide you through the process.
* **Your documents with the bank are not up-to-date**  
Call usand when prompted, say 'update documents' and we'll let you know what you should do.  
If you still need help, call [+971 600 54 0000](tel:971600540000)and when prompted, say 'issue with online/mobile banking' or visit [one of our branches](https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/branches-and-atms), and we'll be happy to help. Please bring your passport or Emirates ID for identification.
title: Unlock your Online and Mobile Banking  | Support | Emirates NBD

text:
Unlock your Online and Mobile Banking  | Support | Emirates NBD > FAQs

## FAQs  
[Why was I locked out of my Online and Mobile Banking?](#faqs-why-was-i-locked-out-of-my-online-mobile-banking "Why was I locked out of my Online and Mobile Banking")  
The most common reasons you can be locked out of your digital banking are:  
* you entered the wrong password or answers to your secret questions multiple times
* your Online or Mobile Banking profile has been compromised
* your documents with the bank are not updated  
For information on what to do about any of these issues, click [here](/en/help-and-support/unlock-your-online-mobile-banking).  
[I’m not sure why I’ve been locked out of my Online and Mobile Banking. How can I find out?](#faqs-im-not-sure-why-ive-been-locked-out-of-my-online-mobile-banking-how-can-i-find-out "Im not sure why Ive been locked out of my Online and Mobile Banking. How can I find out")  
If you attempt to log in to a blocked Online or Mobile Banking profile, information will pop up onscreen stating why your profile has been blocked and how you can unblock it. In addition, when your Online and Mobile Banking profile is blocked because you entered your password or secret question answers incorrectly multiple times, you’ll receive an SMS on your [registered mobile number](/en/help-and-support/update-your-registered-mobile-number)notifying you about the block and the reason for it.

[Should I activate my Online and Mobile Banking profile if it was blocked for security reasons?](#faqs-should-i-activate-my-online-mobile-banking-profile-if-it-was-blocked-for-security-reasons "Should I activate my Online and Mobile Banking profile if it was blocked for security reasons")  
If your Online and Mobile Banking profile was blocked due to security reasons, please call us on [+971 600 54 0000](tel:971600540000)for further assistance. When prompted, say 'issue with online/mobile banking'.

## Quickly and easily access your accounts  
Use our 24-hour automated Phone Banking service to quickly and easily access your accounts and keep yourself up to date wherever you may be.  
Our phone banking agents are available to serve you in English, Arabic and Hindi 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including Sundays and public days. Just call us on [+971 600 540000](tel:+971 600 540000), and we’ll be more than happy to assist you.  
If you have [lost your card and would like to block it](/en/help-and-support/block-your-card), the quickest way to do so is through Online Banking and Mobile Banking.  
If your feel your accounts has been compromised, please call us immediately on [+971 600 540000](tel:+971 600 540000).  
**Note:** The system has a built-in and highly secure authentication mechanism, so you can rest assured that your phone banking transactions are safe and confidential.  
Never divulge your PIN to anyone including Emirates NBD staff or phone banking agents.

## FAQs  
[Who can access the Emirates NBD Phone Banking Service?](#faqs-who-can-access-the-emirates-nbd-phone-banking-service "Who can access the Emirates NBD Phone Banking Service")  
All Emirates NBD customers except jointly held and minor accounts can access the phone banking service.  
[How can I activate my Emirates NBD credit/debit card through Phone Banking?](#faqs-how-can-i-activate-my-emirates-nbd-credit-debit-card-through-phone-banking "How can I activate my Emirates NBD creditdebit card through Phone Banking")  
In order to activate your Emirates NBD credit/debit card, please call us at [+971 600540000](tel:+971 600540000) from your registered mobile number and follow the instructions. This will take you to the activation flow and then you can have the card activated over the call. Alternatively, you can SMS ACT to 4459 from your registered mobile number in order to receive a call back for activating your debit or credit card.  
[How can I redeem my reward points through Phone Banking?](#faqs-how-can-i-redeem-my-reward-points-through-phone-banking "How can I redeem my reward points through Phone Banking")  
No, you can't redeem your reward or Plus points through Phone Banking, but you can easily redeem them through Mobile or Online Banking. To learn more about your rewards, click [here](/en/help-and-support/understanding-your-rewards).
title: Phone Banking | Support | Emirates NBD

text:
Phone Banking | Support | Emirates NBD > FAQs

[How can I update my mobile number via Phone Banking?](#faqs-how-can-i-update-my-mobile-number-via-phone-banking "How can I update my mobile number via Phone Banking")  
Your registered mobile number can't be updated via Phone Banking, but you can easily update it through Mobile Banking or any of our ATMs. To learn more, click [here](/en/help-and-support/update-your-registered-mobile-number)  
[How do I reset my card PIN through Phone Banking](#faqs-how-do-i-reset-my-card-pin-through-phone-banking "How do I reset my card PIN through Phone Banking")  
To reset your credit or debit card pin, [click here.](/en/help-and-support/reset-your-card-pin)  
[Do I need to sign up for the utility bill payment option on Phone Banking?](#faqs-do-i-need-to-sign-up-for-the-utility-bill-payment-option-on-phone-banking "Do I need to sign up for the utility bill payment option on Phone Banking")  
You do not need to register for the utility bill payment option as you can authenticate on Phone Bankingusing your card number and PIN, by calling out the utility for which you wish to make the payment. Payments can be done for registered/unregistered beneficiaries.  
[Can I request an e-statement through Phone Banking?](#faqs-can-i-request-an-estatement-through-phone-banking "Can I request an estatement through Phone Banking")
title: Phone Banking | Support | Emirates NBD

text:
Phone Banking | Support | Emirates NBD > FAQs

Yes, statement requests can be made through Phone Banking for both accounts and cards. The statements will be sent to your [registered email address.](/en/help-and-support/update-your-email-address)  
[Can I pay somebody else's utility bill through Phone Banking?](#faqs-can-i-pay-for-somebody-elses-utility-bill-through-phone-banking "Can I pay somebody elses utility bill through Phone Banking")  
Yes, as long as you have an Emirates NBD debit or credit card and the required utility account number, you may pay someone else's bill. To learn more, [click here.](/en/help-and-support/make-a-utility-payment)  
[Can I make utility payments via Phone Banking?](#faqs-can-i-make-utility-payments-via-phone-banking "Can I make utility payments via Phone Banking")  
Yes, you can make bill payments through phone banking. To learn more, [click here.](/en/help-and-support/make-a-utility-payment)  
[Can I make a telegraphic transfer through Phone Banking?](#faqs-can-i-make-a-telegraphic-transfer-through-phone-banking "Can I make a telegraphic transfer through Phone Banking")  
No, telegraphic transfers cannot be made through Phone Banking. However, you can follow simple steps to make transfer through Online or Mobile banking. To learn more, click [here.](/en/help-and-support/reset-your-card-pin)

## Requirements and documents for opening an account  
[UAE Nationals](#accordion-b2a57099-3e73-4c88-b0d8-6a8c0cd24309 "UAE Nationals")  
* **Identification**
+ Original Emirates ID and copy
+ Copy of passport
* **In case of a salary transfer account, we’ll need one of the following documents:**
+ Copy of Labor Card
+ Copy of Employee ID
+ Latest salary letter
+ Copy of employment visa page from passport  
[Expats](#accordion-49623495-ba62-44dd-a54b-5dd579941ee2 "Expats")  
* **Identification**
+ Original Emirates ID and copy
+ Copy of passport
* **In case of a salary transfer account, we’ll need one of the following documents:**
+ Salary transfer letter (not more than 30 days from date of issue for non-government companies. For government companies, validity as mentioned in the letter.)
+ Copy of appointment letter or contract
+ Copy of payslip (less than 3 months old)
+ Statement with previous month’s salary
+ **For bulk accounts:** consolidated letter from HR (with salary of each employee mentioned)  
[Non-residents](#accordion-cbd4dd43-bd60-41bf-b371-0d4f67de2517 "Nonresidents")  
* **Passport and copy with visa page and one of the following documents**
+ Utility bill (not more than 3 months old)
+ Bank statements (not more than 3 months old and you can print these off online banking too)

# How Wealth Management supports your long-term goals  
14 October 2025  
[Share](javascript:void(0); "Share")  
![howwealthmanagementsupportsyourlongtermgoals](/-/media/enbd/images/knowledge-hub/how_wealth_management_supports_goals.jpg?la=en&h=600&w=800&hash=32C92532B8A84BCA183A0E3D9130EBD1)  
#####  
Most of us have ambitions that go beyond today: providing for children’s education, retiring with confidence, buying a second home, or leaving a legacy. Achieving these milestones takes more than saving. It requires a clear plan, expert guidance and the right tools to grow, protect and transfer wealth.  
At Emirates NBD, we are more than banking: we are your partner in building, growing and protecting your wealth. We recognise that every client’s financial journey is unique, and our [**Wealth Management**](https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/wealth) solutions are designed to match both your near-term priorities and long-term aspirations.  
Here’s how we support you at every stage.
title: How Wealth Management supports your long-term goals
section: How Wealth Management supports your long-term goals

text:
How Wealth Management supports your long-term goals > **1. Retirement planning: securing your future**

## **1. Retirement planning: securing your future**  
When to retire and how much you will need depends on your lifestyle, family and future costs. Our advisers work with you to define your retirement needs and create a plan that balances growth with security, using suitable savings and investment strategies to prepare for tomorrow while supporting today.
title: How Wealth Management supports your long-term goals

text:
How Wealth Management supports your long-term goals > **2. Education funding: investing in opportunity**

## **2. Education funding: investing in opportunity**  
From international schooling in the UAE to universities abroad, education is one of life’s biggest investments. Starting early is key. By steadily investing in a diversified plan that matches when fees fall due, you give your savings the best chance to keep pace with rising costs. Our advisers help structure strategies around your family’s milestones, so opportunities remain within reach.
title: How Wealth Management supports your long-term goals

text:
How Wealth Management supports your long-term goals > **3. Growing wealth through diversification**

## **3. Growing wealth through diversification**  
Wealth building means putting your money to work across the four core asset classes: cash, bonds/sukuk, equities and property. Other solutions, such as mutual funds or structured products, combine exposures to these building blocks to shape outcomes.  
Growth can support both short-term goals such as a property purchase or family wedding and long-term ones such as retirement. A diversified approach helps manage market ups and downs while aiming to outpace inflation over time. Our team can help you build and maintain a portfolio aligned to your objectives, and you can open and manage an investment portfolio directly on the ENBD X app.  
A wise note: uncertainty is certain. Plan ahead. Use time, diversification and disciplined rebalancing to stay on track, and consider structured products where appropriate to target specific risk and return profiles.
title: How Wealth Management supports your long-term goals

text:
How Wealth Management supports your long-term goals > **4. Protecting your wealth against uncertainty**

## **4. Protecting your wealth against uncertainty**  
Life happens. Market downturns, health events or urgent expenses can disrupt even the best-laid plans. We help you build resilience with the right safety nets: liquidity for emergencies and protection solutions with our insurance partners, so your long-term plan stays on course.
title: How Wealth Management supports your long-term goals

text:
How Wealth Management supports your long-term goals > **5. Succession planning**

## **5. Succession planning**  
Wealth is also about what you pass on. From caring for family members to supporting causes you believe in, succession planning is vital. Our specialists work with Ultra High Net Worth Individuals across segments to help structure assets, manage inheritance considerations and transfer wealth smoothly and responsibly.
title: How Wealth Management supports your long-term goals

text:
How Wealth Management supports your long-term goals > **6. Stay in control with ENBD X**

## **6. Stay in control with ENBD X**  
Managing long-term goals takes steady attention. With the [**ENBD X app**](https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/ways-of-banking/mobile-banking), you can open an investment portfolio in minutes, trade local and global equities, and track performance in one place. It is simple, secure and designed around you.  
* If you want more control and speed, you will enjoy fast transfers, access to global markets, and research tools to support your decisions.
* If you value convenience and cost savings, you will benefit from easy digital journeys and 24/7 availability, so you can bank and invest whenever it suits you.

## What are people asking?  
[What is a Loan on Card facility?](#accordion-c9c79208-2b52-4112-a630-44395db14887 "What is a Loan on Card facility")  
The (LOC) facility allows you to convert a portion of your available Credit Card limit into cash. The amount is transferred directly to your bank account or issued as a manager’s cheque.  
[Who can apply for a Loan on Card?](#accordion-15e55bf6-891a-4f12-ae8e-f281e415a6a4 "Who can apply for a Loan on Card")  
This facility is available for primary Emirates NBD credit cardholders, based on your eligibility and available credit limit.  
[What is the maximum amount I can borrow as a Loan on Card?](#accordion-6be44a9d-db3c-4429-8453-7cfb566c7333 "What is the maximum amount I can borrow as a Loan on Card")  
You can borrow up to 90% of your available Credit Card limit, depending on your eligibility and available credit limit.  
[What are the tenure options for 'Loan on Card'?](#accordion-7becaad0-ed2f-43c7-9967-b097477215e6 "What are the tenure options for Loan on Card")  
You can choose to repay your Loan on Card over 12, 18, 24, 36, or 48 months.  
[What is the interest rate for Loan on Card?](#accordion-e4b55fdb-3505-43c1-8bf2-d3134f438360 "What is the interest rate for Loan on Card")  
The interest rate is a reducing monthly rate determined by Emirates NBD and shall be charged on the loan amount. Interest rates are subject to change based on Card usage and performance.

### Borrow wisely – a few things you should know  
* If you don’t make the monthly payments towards your loan on time, you will incur a late payment fee
* Missing repayments can affect your credit score, limiting your ability to access loans or financing in the future
* If you refinance your loan or defer your payments, your loan will take longer to pay back, and you may pay more interest
* If you can’t meet a monthly payment, [apply in advance for a deferment](https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/help-and-support/defer-your-loan-payments). You can do this up to twice a year  
It’s important to read the terms and conditions and know the fees and charges before you apply for a loan.

text:
Liability and No Liability Letter | Help and Support | Emirates NBD > What are Liability and No-liability letters?

## What are Liability and No-liability letters?  
A Liability Letter is an official document that lists and confirms your current financial obligations such as loans and credit cards with the bank. It’s valid for 15 days. A No-liability Letter, on the other hand, confirms you have no liabilities with the bank.

## Request a letter now  
**If you don’t have an Emirates NBD AED account or if you are addressing the letter to a financial institution:** Please visit an[Emirates NBD branch](https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/branches-and-atms)with your Emirates ID or passport for identification, and we’ll be happy to help. Otherwise, proceed with your request using one of the options below.

text:

## What’s next  
Your request will take 6 working days to be processed. You’ll receive an SMS on your [registered mobile number](/en/help-and-support/update-your-registered-mobile-number) once your letter is ready to be collected. Come to your nearest [Emirates NBD branch](/en/branches-and-atms) and remember to bring your Emirates ID or passport for identification.

text:
Liability and No Liability Letter | Help and Support | Emirates NBD > FAQs

## FAQs  
[Can I issue a Liability or No-liability letter addressed to myself?](#faqs-can-i-issue-a-liability-or-no-liability-letter-addressed-to-myself "Can I issue a Liability or Noliability letter addressed to myself")  
Yes, you can issue the letters to your name, however they can’t be addressed to ‘Whom it may concern’.  
[Why do I need a Liability or No-liability letter?](#faqs-why-do-i-need-a-liability-or-no-liability-letter "Why do I need a Liability or Noliability letter")  
You could need this letter for a number of reasons. You might be taking a loan, applying for a new credit card and the bank has requested it, or you may be moving to another country from the UAE and Immigration authorities might need to see it.

# DMCC Corporate Card

## Frequently Asked Questions  
[What is the eligibility to apply for Emirates NBD Business Banking accounts digitally?](#accordion-44d02987-efd0-4ab2-becf-90eec895ace1 "What is the eligibility to apply for Emirates NBD Business Banking accounts digitally")  
It is open to all registered business entities operating in Trading, Manufacturing, Contracting, Transportation and Professional or any of the Service sectors in the UAE, wherein at least one signatory is a UAE resident.  
[What are the 6 most important business banking services?](#accordion-55317a9e-69c1-415d-b920-c040eeadeb87 "What are the 6 most important business banking services")  
There are many important banking services that financial institutions can provide, however, the top 6 to look out for are:  
* **Deposits:** Business banking will be able to help businesses with their day-to-day operations by allowing them to make and receive payments, manage their cash flow, and separate different types of transactions.  
* **Lending:** Business banking can offer all kinds of credit options such as loans, asset-based loans, and other lines of credit to enable businesses to operate and grow.  
* **Treasury and payments:** Businesses often have large sums of money moving in and out of their accounts, so many business bank account providers will provide treasury management services to help businesses manage their cash flow and liquidity.
title: Open Business Bank Account Online in the UAE |  Emirates NBD

text:
Open Business Bank Account Online in the UAE |  Emirates NBD > Frequently Asked Questions

* **Cash Management offerings:** Our efficient and effective cash management solutions cover your regular and routine payments, as well as collections and overall liquidity, empowering you to explore opportunities.  
* **Forex Exchange Solutions:** Many banks now offer international banking services, such as foreign exchange services, or connections to payment systems for secure, fast, international payments.  
* **Trade and Working Capital Finance:** We give you a competitive edge through our full spectrum of trade, working capital and advisory services, to enable you to explore opportunities with confidence at home and overseas.  
[What packages does Emirates NBD offer to its Business Banking customers?](#accordion-beab0348-d902-4648-adc0-c47aa4af713f "What packages does Emirates NBD offer to its Business Banking customers")

* **Lending:** Business banking can offer all kinds of credit options such as loans, asset-based loans, and other lines of credit to enable businesses to operate and grow.

Take care of your family's cash needs by giving them a supplementary debit card and set customised limits for purchases and cash withdrawals. You can apply for as many as 10 supplementary debit cards for your family, including minors (children below 18) and house help.

## Not able to reach us through the above channels?

text:
Apply for A Supplementary Debit Card in Dubai | Support | Emirates NBD > How long it will take

## How long it will take  
Your supplementary debit card application will be processed in 7 working days. Once your application is accepted, your card will be delivered to you in 3 to 5 working days.  
International deliveries may take up to 7 to 10 working days and a fee of 157.50 (inclusive of VAT) will apply.

* Offer not valid in conjunction with any other promotions & discounts.

If you have multiple loans, consider our debt consolidation programme,[One Pay](/en/campaigns/debt-consolidation).
title: Restructure your loan | Support | Emirates NBD

text:
Restructure your loan | Support | Emirates NBD > Speak to us now

## Speak to us now  
Come to your nearest [Emirates NBD branch](https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/branches-and-atms) and we’ll be happy to help. Bring your passport or Emirates ID for identification.  
We’ll review your request and once it’s all approved, you can start paying your new installments from the very next month.
title: Restructure your loan | Support | Emirates NBD

text:
Restructure your loan | Support | Emirates NBD > Consolidate your liabilities – One Pay

## Consolidate your liabilities – One Pay  
If you have multiple loans, including debt on your credit card, we can make your payments easier by clubbing all your debt into one, so you pay just one easy installment every month.  
Our debt consolidation programme, One Pay, makes this possible and also gives you preferential interest rates.  
[Calculate your single monthly payment and apply now.](/en/campaigns/debt-consolidation)
title: Restructure your loan | Support | Emirates NBD

text:
Restructure your loan | Support | Emirates NBD > Fees and charges

## Fees and charges  
You pay a rescheduling fee of 262.5 when you apply for a loan restructure. There are no other fees or charges.
title: Restructure your loan | Support | Emirates NBD

text:
Restructure your loan | Support | Emirates NBD > FAQs

## FAQs  
[What if I have more than one loan, can I apply for a loan restructure?](#faqs-what-if-i-have-more-than-one-loan-can-i-apply-for-a-loan-restructure "What if I have more than one loan can I apply for a loan restructure")  
Yes, you can. You can also club all your loans and pay back in one easy monthly instalment under our debt consolidation programme, [One Pay](https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/loans/debt-consolidation). You could benefit from a discount and reduced interest rates, depending on the terms and conditions at the time you apply. Please visit [one of our branches](/en/branches-and-atms)to know more.  
[Are there any criterion for my loan to be restructured?](#faqs-are-there-any-criterion-for-my-loan-to-be-restructured "Are there any criterion for my loan to be restructured")  
We will consider your loan tenure, the amount you owe the bank and your personal circumstances. To know more, please come to a [branch](https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/branches-and-atms/) and one of our loan experts will help you out.

# Islamic Banking  
## Our Shari'ah Governance  
Emirates NBD ISLAMIC follows a robust Shari’ah governance mechanism to ensure that all our products and services are duly accredited and in line with Shari’ah principles.  
We practice clear policies, procedures and controls that are approved by the Internal Shari’ah Supervision Committee and facilitate business activities in a manner that are always compliant with the Islamic Shari’ah.  
![Fatwas](/-/media/enbd/images/cib/investmentbanking_cib_banner1.jpg?la=en&h=1400&w=1400&hash=B8566F6E57173952085C39854804B80B)  
#### Fatwas  
ISSC issues fatwas and resolutions that are binding upon Emirates NBD.  
[Know more](/en/islamic-banking/our-shariah-governance/fatwas "Fatwas")

Islamic Banking - Shari’ah Governance | Emirates NBD > Internal Shari’ah Supervision Committee

## Internal Shari’ah Supervision Committee  
The Shari'ah governance process is managed through a three-lines of defense approach with an Islamic window, an Internal Shari'ah control unit and an Internal Shari'ah Audit unit. These units ensure Emirates NBD’s Internal Shari'ah Supervision Committee (“ISSC”) is the Bank’s main Shari’ah governance officer. The ISSC operates in accordance with the requirements of the CBUAE and undertakes supervision of all Shari'ah-compliant businesses, activities, products and services. ISSC issues fatwas and resolutions that are binding upon Emirates NBD.  
![Prof dr Mohammad Abdul Rahim Sultan Al Olama](/-/media/enbd/images/islamic-banking/mohammad_abdul_sultan_image.jpg?la=en&h=300&w=300&hash=8AB620C4402E57BF588BCD6A8BB2A36B)

Chairman, Executive member  
Prof. Dr. Mohammad Abdul Rahim Sultan Al Olama is a professor of jurisprudence and its fundamentals at the College of Law at the United Arab Emirates University in Al Ain, in addition to being a certified expert in financial affairs concerning compliance with Islamic Shari’ah principles. Notably, he leads the Shari’ah committee at the Zakat Fund in the United Arab Emirates.

Islamic Banking - Shari’ah Governance | Emirates NBD > Dr. Salim Ali Al-Ali

### Dr. Salim Ali Al-Ali  
Dr. Salim Ali Al-Ali is an assistant professor at the Department of Shari’ah and Islamic Studies at the College of Law at the United Arab Emirates University, where he teaches a spectrum of courses related to Islamic law and Islamic banking. He was educated in the United Kingdom, where he received his PhD in Financial Law from the University of London. He holds a Bachelor’s in Shari’ah (Jurisprudence and its Fundamentals) and a Master’s in Islamic Banking and Finance. Dr. Al-Ali was also a part-time lecturer for the LLM program at the BPP Law School, BPP University, based in London, where he lectured on a broad spectrum of jurisprudence matters, including Islamic, English, and comparative laws.  
Apart from his academic experience, he is a member of the internal Shari’ah Supervisory Committee for a number of institutions offering Islamic financial services including Emirates NBD, HSBC, and Abu Dhabi First Bank. He participated in a number of international conferences on various issues pertaining to the law of Islamic finance, Islamic financial products, and the legal and regulatory aspects of developing Islamic financial markets, including those held by Harvard University and the University of Cambridge. He is an author of a book titled ‘Raising Capital on Sukuk Markets: Structural, Legal and Regulatory Issues’.

Islamic Banking - Shari’ah Governance | Emirates NBD > Dr. Muhammad Qaseem

### Dr. Muhammad Qaseem  
Dr. Muhammad Qaseem is a well-known Shari’ah scholar and Islamic banking expert. He is the Chairman of the Shari’ah Board of Deutsche Bank Malaysia and Emaan Islamic Banking of Silk Bank Ltd. He is also a member of the ISSC of Dubai Islamic Bank, ENBD and some other institutions. Dr. Qaseem has also served as Shari’ah Board member of Central Bank of Pakistan, DFM, ADCB and many other Islamic banks.  
Dr. Qaseem has taught in International Islamic University of Islamabad for more than 2 decades. He has contributed immensely to the growth and regulation of the Islamic banking industry in various capacities. He has also made valuable efforts for dissemination of Islamic banking knowledge through lectures, trainings, seminars, conferences and workshops. He has written numerous articles on Islamic banking issues and developed policies and manuals for Islamic banks.

Islamic Banking - Shari’ah Governance | Emirates NBD > Dr. Amin Fateh

### Dr. Amin Fateh  
Dr. Amin Fateh holds a bachelor’s and Master’s in honourable Hadith, and a PhD in Islamic studies. He has been part of the Islamic Banking industry ever since its early stages in 1988, initially contributing to the Shari’ah compliance function of Kuwait Finance House. Across the years he has work with many of the most prominent Shari’ah scholars in the field. For more than a decade he has lead Islamic Shari’ah advisory Minhaj. He is currently a member of a number of Shari’ah Boards and committees in the UAE and across the world, including ENBD-Islamic, EIB and the AAOIFI Shari’ah Committee in the UAE. He lectured in many universities and is a profound bilingual Islamic Finance trainer who has provided many Islamic Finance training courses across the world.

Islamic Banking - Shari’ah Governance | Emirates NBD > Prof. Dr. Mohammad Abdul Rahim Sultan Al Olama

### Prof. Dr. Mohammad Abdul Rahim Sultan Al Olama  
Prof. Dr. Mohammad Abdul Rahim Sultan Al Olama is a professor of jurisprudence and its fundamentals at the College of Law at the United Arab Emirates University in Al Ain, in addition to being a certified expert in financial affairs concerning compliance with Islamic Shari’ah principles. Notably, he leads the Shari’ah committee at the Zakat Fund in the United Arab Emirates.  
Prof. Dr. Mohammad Abdul Rahim Sultan Al Olama has published books and articles on various jurisprudential topics, particularly Islamic banking in its contemporary form. He has also presented a series of research papers in various international forums and conferences related to this sector. He is a member of a number of Fatwa and Shari’ah supervisory boards for Islamic financial institutions and Takaful companies. These include Emirates Islamic Bank, Dubai Islamic Bank, Takaful House and Mawarid Finance Company.  
Prof. Dr. Mohammad Abdul Rahim Sultan Al Olama holds a PhD in Comparative Islamic Jurisprudence from Umm Al-Qura University in Makkah Al-Mukarramah, in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

Islamic Banking - Shari’ah Governance | Emirates NBD > Dr. Mohamed Ali Elgari

### Dr. Mohamed Ali Elgari  
Dr. Elgari holds the distinction of being a Former Professor of Islamic Economics at King Abdulaziz University, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, and Former Director of the Center for Research in Islamic Economics, at the same university. He is an Expert at the Islamic Jurisprudence Academy of the OIC and the Islamic Jurisprudence Academy of the Islamic World League. Dr. Elgari is also a member of the Board of Trustees of AAOFI as well as their Shari’ah counsel. He is a distinguished member of the editorial board of several academic publications in the field of Islamic Finance and Jurisprudence.  
Dr. Elgari is also chairman and member of numerous Shari’ah boards of Islamic banks and Takaful companies worldwide. He has authored several books in Islamic finance and has published tens of articles on the subject, both in Arabic and English. Dr. Elgari is also a frequent speaker at conferences worldwide. He holds a PhD from the University of California.

[I’ve not received my OTP. What should I do?](#accordion-1fdbbdfb-f81a-443c-9711-d247d51d6222 "Ive not received my OTP. What should I do")

[Is it safe to share my card number?](#accordion-c14e16bd-40cc-461b-87a6-b5f8a7f4570b "Is it safe to share my card number")  
You should avoid sharing any of your bank details with people you don’t know or can’t trust. It’s ok to share this information with the bank in a safe manner.
